works.title: Design, Synthesis, and Herbicidal Activity of Coumarin-3-Acetamide Derivatives as Potential Transketolase Inhibitors
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Transketolase (TKL; EC 2.2.1.1) has been confirmed to be a promising new herbicide target. In this study, two series of the coumarin-based compounds 12a–12j and 13a–13m were designed and synthesized based on TKL as the new target. Among them, compound 12c could significantly inhibit the activity of SvTKL (IC50: 0.96 μmol/L) in vitro. Notably, compound 12c exhibited inhibitory effects of over 90% against D. sanguinalis and A. retroflexus higher than those of the positive control (inhibition < 80%) at 375 g a.i./ ha via the pot spraying method. Additionally, compound 12c exhibited good safety (injury rate <10%) for wheat and maize at 375 g a.i./ha. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation studies indicated that compound 12c has a strong binding ability and dynamic stability with SvTKL. Furthermore, ARG598 may contribute to the stabilization of 12c within the SvTKL active pocket. These findings establish coumarin-fusaric acid derivatives as promising leads for new herbicide development.

works.title: The GID1-DELLA2 Signaling Module Mediates Gibberellin-Induced Seed Germination in Sainfoin ( Onobrychis viciifolia )
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Sainfoin (Onobrychis viciifolia) is an important perennial forage legume, but poor seed germination severely limits its establishment and utilization. Gibberellin (GA) signaling plays a central role in germination; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying GA-mediated germination regulation in sainfoin remain largely unknown. In this study, 11 DELLA family genes were identified, and OvDELLA2 was characterized as a key regulator of seed germination. OvDELLA2 encodes a nucleus-localized protein and is highly induced during germination. Agrobacterium-mediated seed-imbibition transient transformation system was established to facilitate functional analysis in sainfoin. Functional analyses demonstrated that OvDELLA2 overexpression significantly inhibited germination, radicle elongation, and storage reserve mobilization, whereas OvGID1 overexpression enhanced GA responsiveness and promoted germination. Protein interaction assays revealed a GA3-dependent interaction between OvDELLA2 and OvGID1, indicating conservation of the canonical GA-GID1-DELLA signaling module. This study provides insights into GA-regulated seed and offers a platform for functional genomics and molecular breeding in sainfoin.

works.title: Characterization of a Previously Uncharacterized GH43 Arabinofuranosidase with Activity toward O -2 and O -3 Disubstituted Arabinoxylan Oligosaccharides
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Arabinoxylans can be converted by endoxylanases into arabinoxylo-oligosaccharides (AXOS), which require debranching by arabinofuranosidases to yield xylo-oligosaccharides (XOS). However, production of XOS is limited by doubly substituted xylosyl residues which are difficult to debranch. In this study, we identified a previously uncharacterized arabinofuranosidase AsAbf43A (GH43_28) from Alkalitalea saponilacus. Notably, AsAbf43A can remove both the O-2- and O-3-linked arabinosyl substituents from doubly substituted xylosyl residues at the nonreducing ends of arabinoxylo-oligosaccharides (AXOS), a capability rarely reported among characterized GH43 enzymes. The kcat/Km of AsAbf43A was 175.03 ± 37.50 min–1·mM–1 for A2XX and 0.43 ± 0.08 min–1·mM–1 for A2,3XX. Comparison of the AlphaFold model of AsAbf43A with monosubstitution specific BsAXH-m2,3 from Bacillus subtilis suggested an additional pocket adjacent to the −1 subsite which may accommodate the second arabinosyl substituent. This provides a possible structural hypothesis for recognition of disubstituted AXOS.

works.title: FTZ-F1 Homologue Silencing Reveals Endocrine and Xenobiotic-Response Vulnerabilities Associated with RNAi–Insect Growth Regulator Co-Treatment in Heortia vitessoides
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Insect growth regulators disrupt endocrine signaling, but the molecular vulnerabilities underlying their effects remain incompletely understood. Here, two FTZ-F1 homologues in Heortia vitessoides were characterized and functionally analyzed. RNAi-mediated knockdown of either homologue impaired ecdysis, pupation, and adult emergence. HvFTZ-F1–1 knockdown was more strongly associated with reduced fat-body triglyceride content and lipid-metabolism-related transcription, whereas HvFTZ-F1–2 knockdown was more strongly associated with midgut epithelial disruption, reduced ELISA-derived 20E immunoreactive levels, and broader transcriptomic perturbation. Pyriproxyfen and tebufenozide induced opposite transcriptional responses of the two homologues. Chitosan-dsRNA cotreatment produced combination-dependent survival responses, with CS-dsF1+Teb and CS-dsF2+PPF showing reduced survival relative to the corresponding pesticide-control groups. These findings identify homologue-biased developmental vulnerabilities and support a laboratory framework for RNAi–insect growth regulator cotreatment in H. vitessoides.

works.title: Discovery of Novel Aminopyridine Ethers as Promising Auxin Herbicides
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Auxin herbicides are vital for agricultural weed management. To develop novel and efficient auxin herbicides, a series of aminopyridine ether compounds were designed and synthesized via fragment splicing. Postemergence herbicidal activity assays showed that compounds C6, C7, and C8 achieved 100% control against Echinochloa crusgalli (E.c.), Eleusine indica (E.i.), Setaria faberi (S.f.), Amaranthus retroflexus (A.r.), Abutilon juncea (A.j.), and Portulaca oleracea (P.o.) at 37.5 g a.i./ha. Especially, C8 provided over 70% control of all six weeds at 9.375 g a.i./ha. At 75 g a.i./ha, compounds C7 and C8 caused less damage to gramineous crops than fluchloraminopyr-tefuryl. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses demonstrated that C8 alters the expression of genes associated with plant growth, development and stress responses, and disrupts plant growth by interfering with auxin signal transduction and reducing the content of the key metabolite indole-3-acetic acid. The present work indicates that C8 possesses great potential as an auxin-type herbicide for weed control.

works.title: α-Substituent Effects Modulate the Reactivity of C2 Monocarboxylic Acids for Efficient Hemicellulose Removal from Lignocellulose
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Efficient and selective fractionation of lignocellulose is essential for downstream valorization, yet pretreatment with conventional monocarboxylic acids is generally inefficient. The inductive effects of α-substituents in C2 monocarboxylic acids (C2-MCAs) may govern lignocellulose deconstruction, but underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Herein, glyoxylic acid (GoA) pretreatment of Eucalyptus was evaluated and benchmarked against glycolic acid (GcA) and acetic acid (AA). GoA removed 86.21% of hemicellulose (150 °C, 4% GoA, and 30 min) and exhibited the lowest apparent activation energy (12.74 kJ/mol), compared with GcA (59.85 kJ/mol) and AA (124.98 kJ/mol). Electrostatic potential and energy-decomposition analyses indicated enhanced proton-donating ability and the strongest interaction with a lignin-carbohydrate complex (−62.69 kJ/mol) for GoA. This suggested that stronger preassociation may facilitate hemicellulose removal. GoA pretreatment reduced lignin β-O-4 abundance and molecular weight while increasing phenolic hydroxyl content. These findings establish a structure–activity relationship between C2-MCAs and hemicellulose separation, providing a molecular basis for efficient organic-acid pretreatment.

works.title: Probiotic-Derived Extracellular Vesicles as Next-Generation Postbiotics: Biogenesis, Host Interactions, and Translational Challenges
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Probiotic-derived extracellular vesicles (PEVs) are membrane-enclosed particles carrying diverse microbial molecules, with potential as next-generation postbiotic platforms. This review compares vesicle biogenesis and composition across Gram-negative bacteria, Gram-positive bacteria, and probiotic yeasts, emphasizing how producer biology shapes characterization and host interactions. Vesicle uptake, functional cargo delivery, and causal attribution are distinguished to assess evidence for intestinal barrier reinforcement, immune modulation, metabolic effects, and gut-organ communication. Available evidence most consistently supports intestinal barrier protection and innate immune modulation, whereas cargo-specific mechanisms and intact-vesicle trafficking to distal organs remain insufficiently resolved. Mechanistic assessment requires complementary evidence concerning vesicle identity, cargo necessity and rescue, receptor involvement, and biodistribution. Key translational priorities include reproducible production, standardized dose reporting, validated potency assays, and safety evaluation. Together, these considerations provide a basis for evaluating the potential of PEVs as defined postbiotic preparations for food and nutrition applications.

works.title: Mechanistic Insights into the Effects of Structural Characteristics on Lignin Depolymerization in Acidic Deep Eutectic Solvents
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Converting lignin into high-value chemicals is an effective valorization strategy. However, the relationship between lignin structures and their depolymerization behaviors in acidic deep eutectic solvents (DESs) remains unclear. This study characterized hardwood, softwood, and herbaceous lignins and investigated their depolymerization in an acidic DES (choline chloride (ChCl):p-toluenesulfonic acid (p-TsOH)). Results demonstrated that β–O–4 linkage content, which is positively correlated with oil yield, is one of the key determinants of depolymerization extent. Model compound experiments revealed the condensation mechanism of syringyl (S) units in a strongly acidic DES, where S-type aldehyde-containing fragments are highly prone to condensation. Additionally, demethylation of S-type phenolic fragments generates polyphenolic species, further promoting condensation. The depolymerization products exhibited notable antioxidant activity. This work clarifies structure–depolymerization relationships and condensation mechanisms in acidic DESs, offering a theoretical foundation for targeted lignin conversion into aromatic chemicals and polymer precursors.

works.title: Efficient Extracellular Production of Highly Branched β-(1→3,1→6)-Glucan by Engineered Aureobasidium melanogenum
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract β-(1→3,1→6)-Glucan is valued for its immunomodulatory activity, but conventional production via fungal cell wall extraction suffers from complex procedures and low yields. Here, the mangrove-derived strain Aureobasidium melanogenum BZ-11 was engineered by sequentially disrupting the melanin and pullulan biosynthetic pathways, generating the mutant strain BZΔPΔA capable of producing pigment-free, pullulan-free extracellular β-glucan. β-Glucan featured a β-(1→3,1→6)-linked structure with a high molecular weight of (1.33 ± 0.24) × 106 g/mol and a high degree of branching of 57%, along with favorable storage and processing stability. In a 10 L fermentation, BZΔPΔA achieved an extracellular β-glucan titer of 20.33 ± 1.42 g/L. Direct ethanol precipitation and lyophilization from the culture supernatant yielded 94.83% β-glucan purity and 97.78% recovery, enabling simple purification without harsh extraction. This work establishes a scalable and efficient platform for producing structurally defined extracellular β-(1→3,1→6)-glucan, with strong potential for applications in functional foods, pharmaceuticals, and biomedical products.

works.title: Biocontrol of Potato Common Scab by Serratia rubidaea A14 and Characterization of Its Inhibitory Volatile Organic Compounds
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Potato common scab, mainly caused by Streptomyces scabies, is a widespread soil-borne disease that greatly reduces tuber quality and market value. Conventional control strategies are often inadequate or environmentally harmful, necessitating eco-friendly biocontrol alternatives. Here, strain A14, isolated from tea rhizosphere, was identified as Serratia rubidaea via polyphasic taxonomy. In vitro assays demonstrated strong antagonism against S. scabies, with a 25 mm inhibition zone. Pot trials confirmed its biocontrol efficacy of 45.45%. Mechanistic investigation indicated that volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from A14 were responsible for pathogen suppression. GC-MS/MS detected 14 VOCs; 2,4-di-tert-butylphenol (2,4-DTBP), 2-mercapto-4-phenylthiazole (2-MPT), and dimethyl disulfide (DMDS) showed potent inhibitory activity. 2,4-DTBP fully inhibited pathogen growth at 0.05 g/L, and 2-MPT (EC50 = 0.018 g/L) was newly found to be active against streptomycetes. This work identifies S. rubidaea A14 as a promising biocontrol agent and provides novel VOC candidates for developing biofumigants toward sustainable potato scab management.

works.title: Sulfakinin Signaling Regulates Feeding and Energy Homeostasis in Hyphantria cunea : A Viable Target for Oral RNAi-Based Pest Control
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Hyphantria cunea is a globally important pest of agricultural and forest ecosystems, owing its invasiveness to starvation tolerance, high feeding activity, and rapid reproduction. Neuropeptide signaling systems play a central role in regulating these key physiological processes. This study characterized the Sulfakinin (SK)/Sulfakinin receptor (SKR) pathway in H. cuneaand evaluated its potential for pest management. SK and SKR expression was influenced by nutritional status. Silencing SK or SKR disrupted energy homeostasis, increased food consumption, depleted energy reserves, reduced stress tolerance, and severely impaired reproduction. Conversely, SK peptide injection suppressed feeding during the early treatment period and significantly limited larval weight gain at 48–72 h. Furthermore, oral delivery of bacterially produced dsRNA targeting SK or SKR induced RNAi responses, resulting in increased larval mortality and delayed development. Collectively, these findings highlight the SK/SKR signaling pathway as a promising molecular target for sustainable RNAi-based strategies to control H. cunea.

works.title: Natural Product-Inspired Scaffold Hopping from Nicotlactone A to Phthalides: Discovery of Potent Antiviral Agents against Plant Viruses
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Natural products are valuable sources of environmentally friendly pesticides. Inspired by nicotlactone A, a series of phthalide derivatives (A1–A24, B1–B9, and C1–C9) were designed and synthesized via scaffold hopping and evaluated for in vivo antiviral activity. Most compounds showed good to excellent activity against Tobacco mosaic virus (TMV). Compound C2 exhibited the most potent TMV inactivation, with a half maximal effective concentration (EC50) of 182.5 mg/L, lower than that of ningnanmycin (EC50 = 202.5 mg/L) and ribavirin (EC50 = 296.8 mg/L). C2 also displayed protective effects against Potato virus Y (PVY, 59.4%) and Zucchini yellow mosaic virus (ZYMV, 58.0%), comparable to ningnanmycin at 500 mg/L. Mechanistic studies revealed that C2 disrupts TMV virion morphology, binds to the viral coat protein (Kd = 2.21 μM), and impedes viral proliferation and movement in plants, highlighting C2 as a promising broad-spectrum antiviral candidate for further development.

works.title: Functional Characterization and Structure-Guided Mutational Analysis of PgUGT71B20, a Flavonoid Glycosyltransferase from Platycodon grandiflorus
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract UDP-glycosyltransferases (UGTs) contribute to plant metabolite diversity, but predicting their substrate specificity and catalytic efficiency remains challenging. By conducting tissue-specific metabolite profiling, transcriptome analysis, and genome-wide UGT screening, we identified PgUGT71B20 from Platycodon grandiflorus. Biochemical characterization showed that PgUGT71B20 uses UDP-glucose to glucosylate quercetin at the 3-O position. Substrate profiling revealed a preference for flavonols and dihydroflavonols with an available 3-hydroxyl group, while flavones, flavanones, isoflavones, and flavanols were poorly converted. Among six sugar donors tested, the enzyme displayed a strong preference for UDP-glucose, with only weak activity for UDP-xylose. Docking and alanine-scanning mutagenesis identified H17 and N308 as essential catalytic residues, whereas D181 modulated catalytic performance. D181A increased catalytic efficiency by reducing the apparent Km for quercetin, increasing kcat/Km from 535.20 to 686.21 L mol–1 s–1. MD and MM/PBSA analyses suggested enhanced complex stability and substrate binding. This study provides mechanistic insights into flavonoid 3-O-glycosylation by plant UGTs.

works.title: NaCl-Mediated Multilevel Regulation of Astaxanthin Biosynthesis in Haematococcus lacustris under High-Light Stress: Multiomics Mechanism Elucidation and Industrial-Scale Validation of Astaxanthin Production
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Natural astaxanthin from Haematococcus lacustris is a high-value food ingredient, but its production is hindered by a growth-yield trade-off. Salinity stress is widely used to increase astaxanthin synthesis. However, the adaptive mechanisms and industrial scalability remain poorly characterized. Multiomics and chemical genetics were employed to dissect NaCl-induced regulation and validate the findings in 2 ton outdoor photobioreactors. An optimal concentration of 1 g/L NaCl increased the biomass, astaxanthin content, and productivity by 21.6, 35.0, and 62.4%, respectively, compared to high-light alone. Mechanistically, NaCl triggered cell wall thickening, membrane remodeling, and metabolic reprogramming, which were orchestrated by phytohormones and calcium signaling. Exogenous abscisic acid and γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) further increased yields, with GABA confirmed as a cost-effective industrial inducer. This work advances beyond prior studies by providing systematic industrial-scale validation and a comprehensive multilevel regulatory framework, offering scalable strategies for sustainable microalgal biotechnology.

works.title: tert -Butylquinone Induced Colitis-like Injury in C57BL/6 Mice Accompanied by MAPK/NF-κB Activation, Gut Microbiota Dysbiosis, and Metabolic Disturbances
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract tert-Butylquinone (TBBQ), an oxidation product of the food antioxidant tert-butylhydroquinone (TBHQ), has shown high cellular toxicity, but its intestinal toxicity in vivo remains unclear. Here, C57BL/6 mice were orally administered TBBQ (50, 100, or 200 mg/kg bw) for 7 days, with DSS used as a colitis control. TBBQ caused body weight loss, increased disease activity index, colon shortening, histological injury, intestinal permeability, oxidative stress, and pro-inflammatory cytokine release. High-dose TBBQ markedly reduced ZO-1 and Occludin expression. Western blotting showed increased phosphorylation of MAPK/NF-κB proteins, while network toxicology and molecular docking predicted possible pathway associations. 16S rRNA sequencing and untargeted metabolomics further revealed gut microbiota dysbiosis and amino acid metabolic disturbances. These findings suggest that acute TBBQ exposure can induce colitis-like injury with inflammatory signaling and barrier disruption, accompanied by imbalance in microbiota metabolism, highlighting a potential food-safety concern associated with TBHQ oxidation under high-risk exposure conditions.

works.title: Sequential Engineering of 4-Hydroxyphenylpyruvate Dioxygenase for Enhanced Mesotrione Tolerance in Rice
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Mesotrione (MST) is a highly effective HPPD-inhibiting herbicide, yet rice sensitivity restricts its application in paddy fields. Although numerous HPPD variants conferring herbicide resistance have been identified, optimizing their catalytic performance remains underexplored. Here, the F378S mutant was used as a scaffold for sequential engineering. Targeted mutagenesis of conformationally flexible regions yielded the F378S/S434H double mutant. Compared to F378S, this variant showed further enhanced MST resistance and improved catalytic turnover. Its half-maximal inhibitory concentration reached 6.99 μM, approximately 13-fold higher than that of the wild-type enzyme. Introducing this allele into the endogenous rice OsHPPD locus via prime editing improved MST tolerance, with edited plants growing relatively normally at 180 g a.i. ha–1. Collectively, sequential engineering of resistance-associated HPPD variants can optimize both herbicide tolerance and catalytic properties, providing a promising allele for developing MST-tolerant rice.

Targeting bacterial signaling pathways: a paradigm shift in antimicrobial strategies for food safety
works.journal: Critical Reviews in Food Science and Nutrition
works.abstract: Foodborne bacterial contamination represents a critical challenge to global food safety and public health. Pathogenic bacteria cause millions of foodborne illnesses annually, while spoilage organisms lead to substantial economic losses through product deterioration. Nearly one in ten people worldwide contract foodborne illnesses each year, resulting in approximately 420,000 deaths annually. US$ 110 billion is lost each year in productivity and medical expenses resulting from unsafe food in low and middle-income countries. Conventional preservation methods face limitations including quality degradation, residual toxicity, and growing consumer demand for clean-label solutions. Bacterial signaling pathways orchestrate virulence, biofilm formation, and stress adaptation, offering novel anti-virulence targets that preserve food quality while minimizing microbial hazards. This review systematically examines three major bacterial signaling pathways as novel targets for food antimicrobial strategies. Emerging intervention platforms are evaluated, including computational biology, nanotechnology, synthetic biology, natural QS inhibitors, and enzymatic degradation strategies, with emphasis on practical applications in cold chain, fermented foods, and meat products. Targeting signaling pathways demonstrates significant potential for controlling pathogens. Key challenges include signal molecule stability in food matrices, bioavailability optimization. Multi-target intervention strategies combining computational screening, natural inhibitors, and engineered delivery systems represent the most promising direction for next-generation food antimicrobials.

Microbial Bioprocessing of Plant-Based Food Matrices: From Conventional Analysis to In Situ Characterization of Cell Wall-Bound Phenolic Release
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract The release mechanisms of bound phenolics (BPs) from plant cell walls during bioprocessing, such as microbial fermentation, are highly dynamic and exhibit microscopic spatial selectivity. While conventional chemical analysis can provide macroscopic data on BPs release, it fails to reveal the microscopic spatial heterogeneity and causal relationships underlying the cell wall degradation process. This review examines both conventional extraction-based analytical methods and emerging in situ imaging technologies, such as Raman/FTIR spectroscopy, confocal laser scanning microscopy, immunofluorescence, and mass spectrometry imaging, highlighting their complementary roles and current technical bottlenecks in characterizing BPs release and cell wall degradation. Furthermore, a unified multiscale, multimodal framework is proposed, integrating high-resolution imaging, dynamic fluorescence probes, multidimensional spectroscopy, and machine-learning-assisted data fusion. This holistic characterization strategy elucidates the precise mechanisms governing phenolic release, providing a theoretical basis to guide the targeted enrichment of BPs and advance the efficient utilization of plant biomass and agricultural residues.

works.title: Selection and Application of an Aptamer for the Extraction and HPLC-MS/MS Determination of Six Perfluorinated Compounds in Food
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Recognition elements capable of recognizing multiple PFAS are needed for monitoring PFAS in food. Using Capture-SELEX with PFOA, PFOS, PFNA, and PFHxS as the selection targets, we isolated aptamer S1, which recognized these four compounds as well as PFHpA and PFHpS. Molecular docking and circular dichroism spectroscopy revealed the shared and differential binding sites of S1 with these six PFAS, elucidating the structural basis for their recognition. S1 was immobilized onto streptavidin-coated magnetic beads to construct an Apt-MBs enrichment platform coupled with HPLC-MS/MS. The method exhibited linearity from 0.067 to 50 ng/mL (R2 > 0.997), low detection limits of 0.020–0.050 ng/mL, recoveries of 71.9%–99.3% in spiked meat samples, and relative standard deviations below 6%. This enrichment-LC-MS/MS dual-mode strategy provides a selective, sensitive, and stable tool for monitoring multicomponent PFAS in complex food matrices, with promising applications in nutritional safety assessment and dietary exposure monitoring.

works.title: Autocatalytic CRISPR/Cas12a-Enabled Fluorescence Polarization for Highly Sensitive Detection of Escherichia coli across Diverse Food Matrices
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Rapid and sensitive detection of bacterial contamination in complex food matrices is essential for food safety monitoring. Here, we report an autocatalytic CRISPR/Cas12a-enabled fluorescence polarization (FP) assay for Escherichia coli (E. coli) detection. Following recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA), target amplicons activate Cas12a to cleave a switchable dual-loop reporter (SDL-Reporter). Cleavage releases small fluorescent fragments with enhanced rotational diffusion, decreasing FP, while simultaneously liberating functional crRNA that recruits additional Cas12a for recursive Cas12a activation. This dual-functional design couples feedback amplification with rotational diffusion-based FP transduction. The assay achieved a detection limit of 5 CFU/mL, a linear range of 1.8 × 101 to 1.8 × 107 CFU/mL, and high specificity toward E. coli. Evaluation in 11 pretreated food matrices covering fruits, vegetables, meats, and dairy products demonstrated satisfactory analytical accuracy and reproducibility across different food types. These findings support the potential of the proposed strategy for sensitive foodborne bacterial analysis.

works.title: Isolation and Characterization of a Resveratrol-Metabolizing Human Gut Bacterium
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Resveratrol undergoes biotransformation by gut bacteria, producing metabolites that can contribute to its bioactive potential. Yet the few known intestinal strains contributing to this interaction mainly belong to Coriobacteriia, with only a fraction of them isolated from human feces. Human stool samples (n = 8) were screened, with analytes quantified under liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry. Only one sample produced 3,4′-dihydroxy-trans-stilbene, whereas dihydroresveratrol was detected in all samples, reflecting interindividual variation in resveratrol metabolism across individuals. A bacterium displaying resveratrol-metabolizing capabilities was isolated, producing dihydroresveratrol. Whole genome sequencing identified the isolate as Enterococcus lactis UMA_R1. Time-course analysis revealed that the isolate commenced resveratrol metabolism upon entering the stationary growth phase at 4 h. Broader polyphenol substrate testing suggests that E. lactis UMA_R1 favors reduction of trans-aliphatic or side-chain C═C bonds, with limited activity toward constrained flavonoid structures. These findings advance our knowledge on the key players of resveratrol metabolism in the gut microbiome.

works.title: CsbHLH24 and CsMYB59 Influence Terpenoid Biosynthesis in Tea ( Camellia sinensis ) by Regulating CsTPS Gene Expression
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Volatile terpenoids are important components for tea aroma quality. The molecular mechanism for volatile terpenoid production in tea plants is unknown. In this study, CsbHLH24 and CsMYB59 from Camellia sinensis were functionally characterized. CsbHLH24 was predominantly expressed in tea variety “Zhenfeng Yesheng tea” (ZFYS) and highly correlated with the volatile terpene content and CsTPSs expression. The protein–protein interaction network, molecular docking, yeast two-hybrid assay, and bimolecular fluorescence complementation demonstrated that CsMYB59 directly interacted with CsbHLH24. DNA affinity purification sequencing revealed the cotarget genes of CsbHLH24/CsMYB59 proteins. CsbHLH24 and CsMYB59 were synchronously expressed with CsTPS01 and CsTPS15 and activated their expression. Transient silencing and overexpression of CsbHLH24 and CsMYB59 demonstrated their transcriptional regulatory functions on CsTPS01–CsTPS15 genes and floral terpenoids. These results suggest that the MYB–bHLH complex plays a role in the regulation of CsTPSs, thereby providing a theoretical basis for the terpenoid metabolism regulation and modification.

works.title: Multipesticide Residues in Urban Tap Water across the Yangtze River Delta, China: Hazard-Based Prioritization, Regional Distribution, and Health Risk Assessment
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Pesticide residues in drinking water are an increasing concern in the Yangtze River Delta, yet region-wide assessments remain limited. Herein, 244 widely used pesticides were investigated in tap water collected from 16 cities to characterize their occurrence, spatial distribution, hazard-based prioritization, and health risks. A total of 189 pesticides were detected, including 34 compounds with detection frequencies exceeding 50%. Although pesticide concentrations were generally below guideline values, a prioritization framework integrating exposure potential, persistence, bioaccumulation, and toxicity identified 10 high-priority pesticides. Spatially, pesticide concentrations were significantly higher in Shanghai (46.68 ng/L) and southern Jiangsu (34.91 ng/L) compared with Zhejiang (13.61–21.09 ng/L), associated with differences in agricultural land use and topographic conditions. Although infants exhibited the highest estimated daily intakes, cumulative hazard quotients for all populations remained below 1, indicating acceptable noncarcinogenic risk. These findings provide a region-wide integrated assessment of pesticide contamination in tap water, supporting risk-informed water-quality management.

works.title: Development of a Biomimetic Mucosal Pellicle Model for the Objective Quantification of Polyphenol-Induced Astringency in Model Wine
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Modulating astringency is crucial for enhancing the consumer appeal of polyphenol-rich products. Conventional methods struggle to provide objective quantification, while sensory evaluation is prone to fatigue and subjective bias. Here, we established a biomimetic mucosal pellicle model by loading salivary proteins onto MUC1-overexpressing HSC-3 cells. Then, a high-throughput fluorometric quantification method using Thioflavin T was developed to monitor and quantify the polyphenol-protein aggregates in situ. This model successfully quantified the aggregation potency of key polyphenols, including tannic acid, epigallocatechin gallate, and epigallocatechin. Notably, our results revealed that interfacial protein aggregation followed a sigmoidal transition, characterizing a concentration-dependent progression of mucosal protein aggregation. Sensory evaluation scores strongly correlated with the model measurements (Pearson r = 0.95), confirming the high validity of our method. This biomimetic model establishes a new paradigm for physiologically relevant astringency analysis and provides a scientific basis for the rational design and sensory optimization of polyphenol-rich foods.

works.title: Chlormequat Chloride Disrupts Testicular Cholesterol Homeostasis and Testosterone Synthesis in Peripubertal Rats: Involvement of the miR-212–5p/STARD7 Axis
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Chlormequat chloride (CCC), a widely used plant growth regulator and suspected endocrine disruptor, has been reported to reduce testosterone in peripubertal rats, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, CCC accumulated dose-dependently in the testes of peripubertal rats, accompanied by reductions in testicular cholesterol and testosterone. In H295R cells, CCC impaired cholesterol uptake and testosterone secretion while downregulating LDLR, StAR, VDAC1, STARD7, and CYP11A1. CCC also upregulated miR-212–5p, which directly targeted the STARD7 3′-UTR at a conserved binding site, as shown by dual-luciferase reporter assays. Inhibition of miR-212–5p partially restored testosterone secretion, whereas STARD7 knockdown further reduced testosterone production under CCC exposure. These findings nominate the miR-212–5p/STARD7 axis as a plausible post-transcriptional node contributing to CCC-induced disruption of cholesterol homeostasis and testosterone synthesis, while the causal relevance of this axis in vivo and direct evidence for impaired mitochondrial cholesterol trafficking remain to be established.

works.title: Substrate Versatility and Regiocontrol of Licorice Flavonoid Prenyltransferase GgFPT3 for the Biosynthesis of Diverse Prenylated Flavonoid Natural Products
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Species of Glycyrrhiza (licorice) produce a diverse array of bioactive prenylated flavonoids. Prenyltransferases (PTs) are crucial for this structural diversification, yet their diversity and functional roles in licorice remain largely unexplored. Here, we identified three root-specific, stress-induced flavonoid PT candidates (GgFPT1-3) from G. glabra. While all three mainly localized to the chloroplast, only GgFPT3 exhibited catalytic activity in vitro under the assay conditions tested. GgFPT3 demonstrated remarkable substrate promiscuity, catalyzing the monoprenylation of diverse backbones including dihydroflavones, isoflavans, isoflavanones, isoflavones, chalcones, and pterocarpans, with a regioselective preference for B-ring (e.g., C-3′) prenylation. Intriguingly, despite sharing high amino acid sequence identity (>90%) with GgFPT3, its orthologs in G. inflata and G. uralensis showed distinct expression patterns, enzymatic activities, and substrate preferences. These functional divergences likely underpin the species-specific chemotypic variations of prenylated flavonoids across the Glycyrrhiza genus, expanding our understanding of flavonoid diversification mechanisms.

works.title: Transporter-Modulating Anthocyanin Nanoparticles for Stabilized and Efficient Delivery
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Anthocyanins (ACNs) exhibit poor stability and low bioavailability. These limitations restrict their functional activity and applications in food processing. In this study, we prepared ACNs-loaded nanoparticles by synthesizing thiolated hyaluronic acid and assembling THA/FA-zein@ACNs. The nanoparticles showed a uniform spherical shape with a size of 91.35 nm (PDI = 0.154 ± 0.023) and exhibited robust stability against processing and digestive stress. Caco-2 assays revealed their specific affinity for sodium-glucose cotransporter 1 (SGLT1), enabling active recognition, with SGLT1-mediated uptake being 2.3-fold higher than that mediated by glucose transporter 2 (GLUT2). The system showed reduced P-glycoprotein (P-gp)-mediated efflux, supporting a proposed “push–pull” transport model that maximizes absorption. Free ACNs exhibited a short half-life (0.528 ± 0.105) h, while THA/FA-zein@ACNs prolonged T1/2 to (1.611 ± 0.372) h. The nanoparticles also modulated gut microbiota composition and predicted microbial metabolic functions. This work provides a theoretical and practical foundation for the precise, high-efficiency delivery of functional bioactives.

works.title: Single-Molecule Detection of Lactoferrin and Osteopontin in Infant Formula and Dairy Products Using FraC Nanopores
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Biological nanopore technology enables single-molecule analysis with promising applications in food quality control. Among dairy-derived bioactive components, lactoferrin (LF) and osteopontin (OPN) are two pivotal whey glycoproteins that support infant development and serve as quality indicators for dairy products. However, their folded tertiary structures and heterogeneous charge distributions complicate accurate analysis of these native proteins. Here, we developed a high-resolution nanopore sensing platform utilizing the conical biological nanopore Fragaceatoxin C (FraC), enabling simultaneous qualitative and quantitative analysis of LF and OPN. The platform distinguished and quantified both proteins in mixtures at varying ratios. It also enabled rapid, label-free detection and quantification in commercial dairy products, including infant formula, without chromatographic separation or complicated sample pretreatment. These findings establish a robust theoretical foundation and practical validation for nanopore technology in food quality control, while opening technical avenues for on-site, real-time monitoring of key functional proteins in dairy products, particularly infant formula.

works.title: Engineering a Rieske-Type Oxygenase Enables O -Demethylation of Ferulic Acid to Synthesize Caffeic Acid
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Ferulic acid is a crucial lignin-derived component that serves as a feedstock for the synthesis of multiple high-value compounds through biological conversion. However, the absence of a ferulate O-demethylase restricts wider applications of ferulate. In this study, a Rieske oxygenase, vanillate O-demtheylase (VanAB), which catalyzes vanillate O-demethylation, was used to achieve ferulate O-demethylation via enzyme engineering. Based on the structure of wild-type VanA, the key amino acid residues at the catalytic site were substituted with residues bearing small R groups to allow ferulate to enter. After screening multiple mutants, the VanAQ167A/D171A mutant exhibited the best catalytic performance toward ferulate. Structural insights revealed that the mutant VanAQ167A/D171A had a broadened catalytic site that allowed ferulate entry. Future engineering directions were proposed based on further structural analyses. This study provides a potential route for the biological valorization of ferulic acid to produce caffeic acid and offers valuable insights for engineering Rieske-type oxygenases.

works.title: Cyclotides Enable the Oral Activity of Neuroactive Peptides against Lepidopteran Pests
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Farmers face shrinking crop-protection options due to climate change, resistance, regulations, and demand for residue-free food. Peptides and proteins are attractive solutions because they are potent, specific, and degrade into harmless amino acids. Venom-derived peptide neurotoxins show strong potential as bioinsecticides, but their poor oral activity limits use in sprayable formulations. We show that plant cyclotides, kalata B1 and B2, dramatically enhance the oral efficacy of venom-derived neurotoxins against major lepidopteran pests. Their effects are synergistic, increasing activity by two to 3-fold beyond additivity, and in some cases, enabling complete mortality at doses where either component alone is ineffective. The proposed mechanism involves cyclotides selectively disrupt the lepidopteran midgut barrier, allowing neurotoxins to cross into the hemocoel and act on the nervous system. Microscopy confirms midgut damage, and the D-form of kalata B1 retains activity, indicating an achiral, lipid-mediated interaction. These results establish cyclotides as enablers of peptide-based bioinsecticides against selected important crop pests.

works.title: Advances in Cystathionine β-Lyase-Catalyzed Synthesis of Thiosulfinates: Enzyme Resource Mining, Catalytic Mechanism, and Structure-Guided Molecular Engineering
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Thiosulfinates, represented by diallyl thiosulfinate (allicin), are the material basis of the characteristic flavor and bioactivity of Allium plants. They show broad-spectrum antibacterial, antibiofilm, antiviral, and antitumor activities. However, their extreme chemical instability challenges conventional plant extraction and chemical synthesis. In situ enzymatic synthesis, in which alliinase (l-cysteine sulfoxide lyase, CSL) generates thiosulfinates on demand from S-alk(en)yl-l-cysteine sulfoxide substrates, offers a new solution. Plant-derived CSLs are limited by difficult extraction and low heterologous expression efficiency, whereas bacterial cystathionine β-lyase (CBL), which is easily expressed at low cost, has emerged as a novel catalyst for thiosulfinate biosynthesis. This review summarizes thiosulfinate chemistry and biosynthesis, the structure and pyridoxal phosphate (PLP)-dependent catalysis of CBL, and the discovery of CBL’s CSL activity. Aiming at future food, agricultural, and pharmaceutical applications, we further analyze CBL’s bottlenecks in substrate stereoselectivity and pH preference, highlighting enzyme resource mining and molecular engineering strategies.

works.title: Trypsin-Mediated Control of Metabolic Flux Sustains Detoxification and Reproduction under Chronic Thermal Stress
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Global warming and intensive insecticide use impose concurrent demands on pests, yet mechanisms coordinating resource allocation between stress responses and life-history traits remain poorly understood. We identify midgut trypsins as key regulators of this coordination in the diamondback moth, Plutella xylostella. Using CRISPR/Cas9, we show that two trypsin genes, PxTryCFT1-like and PxTry-like, are dispensable for acute thermal tolerance but essential under chronic stress. Mutant lines exhibit severe reproductive failure under prolonged high temperatures and display broad-spectrum hypersensitivity (2- to 22-fold) to multiple insecticides. Mechanistically, trypsin loss disrupts amino acid supply, suppressing major detoxification systems including cytochrome P450s, glutathione S-transferases, and carboxylesterases. By elucidating the noncanonical role of midgut trypsins in modulating trade-offs between growth and stress defense, we demonstrate how nutrient acquisition fuels stress-response networks.

works.title: Effects of an indigenous Lactiplantibacillus plantarum ST starter on microbial function and metabolic profiling of De’ang pickled tea
works.abstract: This study used metagenomics, untargeted metabolomics, and flavoromics to investigate the effects of the indigenous strain Lactiplantibacillus plantarum ST as a starter on the microbial community and metabolite profiles during the fermentation of De’ang pickled tea. The results showed that after ST inoculation, the microbial interaction network and the relative abundance of rare taxa in the pickled tea changed, accompanied by enrichment of genes related to amino acid metabolism pathways. Metabolomics showed that after ST inoculation, amino acids and their derivatives increased, while the volatile metabolite profile changed, with increases in compounds with pleasant fruity and floral notes and decreases in compounds related to musty and waxy odors. Metabolic pathway prediction further suggested that these metabolic changes may be related to the increased relative abundance of rare taxa such as Sphingomonas sp. and Chryseobacterium camelliae . Overall, L. plantarum ST may shape the metabolic and flavor characteristics during De’ang pickled tea fermentation by affecting the microbial community structure and functional potential. These findings provide a theoretical basis for using indigenous L. plantarum as a starter to regulate quality formation in De’ang pickled tea.

works.title: First application of an integrated microbiological and (meta)genomics approach to verify the biological origin and microbial safety of rennet products
works.abstract: Rennet is essential for cheese production, containing milk-clotting enzymes derived from animal, plant, or microbial sources. Accurate labelling of rennet’s biological origin is essential to respect consumer dietary choices, while microbial contamination may pose food safety risks. We developed an integrated strategy combining qPCR, metagenomics, culture-based methods, whole-genome sequencing, and mass spectrometry to verify the biological origin and microbial safety of 27 commercial products labelled as being of animal ( n = 11), plant ( n = 3), or microbial ( n = 13) origin. DNA matching the labelled production organism was detected in most products, although DNA belonging to other known rennet-producing organisms was also found in several products, including one plant-labelled product containing animal DNA. Additionally, viable B. cereus s.l. was detected in some animal rennet products. To evaluate the potential food safety impact of B. cereus s.l. contamination, rennet products were used to produce cheeses, analysed for B. cereus s.l. growth and cereulide. Bacterial growth and measurable cereulide levels were observed in one cheese, confirming potential food safety risks. To the best of our knowledge, this study provides the first integrated assessment of commercial rennet combining both conventional methods and (meta)genomics, demonstrating the potential of these approaches to identify authenticity issues and microbial safety risks.

Tau-Fluvalinate Inhibits the Molting Process of Lizards ( Eremias argus ) by Disrupting Thyroid Hormone Signaling
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Molting is a critical physiological process essential for lizard growth and survival, primarily regulated by the thyroid system. The potential risks of pyrethroids, as known thyroid disruptors, on ecdysis in lizards remain poorly understood. This study examined the impact of Tau-fluvalinate (FA) on the molting process of lizard (Eremias argus) at 1, 5, and 50 mg/kg soil doses. High-dose FA exposure reduced the incidence of skin shedding and prolonged the ecdysis duration in lizards. Histopathological analysis revealed a significant dose-dependent reduction in the thickness of live strata in lizard skin, along with significant alterations in the key ecdysone-regulated genes in the FA-exposed groups. Mechanistically, FA inhibits molting dynamics and skin cell proliferation as a potential thyroid receptor antagonist by disrupting thyroid hormone signaling. Given the importance of molting for lizard survival, these findings highlight the need to reevaluate the ecological risks of thyroid-disrupting pesticides on lizards.

works.title: Acute Total Ammonia Nitrogen Exposure in Pacific White Shrimp ( Litopenaeus vanname i): Physiological and Multi-Omics Responses Associated with Tissue Semicarbazide
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Acute total ammonia nitrogen (TAN) exposure may impair shrimp health, while the interpretation of semicarbazide (SEM) in crustaceans remains uncertain. We examined physiological, histological, omics, and SEM responses to a 96 h toxicity assay and a 48 h graded TAN challenge (0–20 mg/L), with end point hepatopancreas metabolomics and transcriptomics in the control and 20 mg/L groups. The 96 h LC50 was 24.43 mg/L TAN. High TAN caused gill and hepatopancreas lesions, increased apoptosis, and altered amino acid, purine, energy, lipid, and immune-related profiles. SEM was detectable in shell and gill, including control shell, but not in muscle or hepatopancreas under the analytical conditions used. Shell SEM was associated with several stress indices, and nor-NOHA treatment and in vitro oxidation provided exploratory evidence consistent with a possible role of arginine-related metabolism. These data are consistent with a transition from adaptation to injury and endogenous SEM formation under acute TAN stress.

works.title: Molecular Basis for Altered Hydrolysis and Transglycosylation in a GH20 β- N -Acetylhexosaminidase Mutant: Insights from Molecular Dynamics Simulations
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract β-N-acetylhexosaminidase (NAHase) plays a critical role in the potential high-value transformation of chitin through its hydrolysis and transglycosylation activities. In this work, a novel GH20 NAHase (designated Fmhex) from Fulvivirga maritima was heterologously expressed and biochemically characterized, which showed the highest activity at 45 °C and pH 6.0. To regulate its catalytic properties, a saturated mutation library targeting five nonconserved residues was constructed. Mutants Fmhex(G417A) and Fmhex(I436S) demonstrated 2.3-fold hydrolysis activity and 1.9-fold transglycosylation activity, respectively. Classical molecular dynamics alone cannot fully explain the enhanced hydrolysis of Fmhex(G417A) since it only exhibited a shorter catalytic distance and increased sugar-ring distortion, without a complete near-attack geometry or binding advantage. Conversely, Fmhex(I436S) reshaped the internal pocket architecture, enabling more pocket contacts and hydrogen bonds, deeper burial, and more favorable energetics, providing a structural rationale for its enhanced transglycosylation. These findings provided mechanistic insights and testable hypotheses for engineering NAHases with tailored hydrolysis/transglycosylation balances.

works.title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Metabolomic Analysis Elucidates Melatonin-Mediated Cold and Drought Tolerance during Grapevine Cane Overwintering
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Cold-drought stress limits grapevine cane overwintering. Melatonin is known to enhance plant stress tolerance, but its regulatory mechanisms under natural overwintering remain unclear. We used the new grapevine line “140902” to investigate molecular responses to exogenous melatonin under combined cold-drought stress via integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses. Melatonin increased endogenous hormones and antioxidant enzyme activities (e.g., SOD activity increased 23.6% under M3) and reduced MDA content by up to 31.9%, alleviating physiological damage. DEGs and DAMs were enriched in phenylpropanoid/flavonoid biosynthesis, hormone signaling, and starch/sucrose metabolism pathways. Melatonin upregulated JA/ABA signaling genes (GH3, JAZ, PYL), phenylpropanoid/flavonoid biosynthetic genes (C4H, 4CL, CAD, FLS), and carbon metabolism genes (β-glucosidase, cellulase), altering flavonoid (naringenin, eriodictyol) relative abundance. These coordinated changes may contribute to the melatonin-mediated alleviation of cold-drought injury in grapevines, offering insights into potential regulatory networks and a basis for nonburial cultivation in cold, arid northwestern China.

works.title: Xylo-Oligosaccharides Attenuate T-2 Toxin-Induced Pulmonary Fibrosis by Inhibiting Intestinal Overgrowth and Gut-to-Lung Translocation of Staphylococcus saprophyticus
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract T-2 toxin, a widespread mycotoxin frequently detected in food and feed, severely threatens public health and livestock breeding safety. Although reports indicate its potential to cause pulmonary injury, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we demonstrated that T-2 toxin compromised intestinal barrier integrity and increased abundance of S. saprophyticus in both the ileum and the lungs, thereby triggering pulmonary inflammation and fibrosis in piglets and mice. Transplantation of fecal microbiota from T-2 toxin-exposed piglets into recipient piglets mimicked the phenomena. NOD2 gene knockdown in mice reversed S. saprophyticus-induced pulmonary damage. Besides, xylo-oligosaccharides (XOS) inhibited the proliferation of S. saprophyticus driven by T-2 toxin and its translocation from the ileum to the lungs, thereby suppressing the NOD2/NF-κB signaling pathway and ultimately alleviating pulmonary fibrosis. This study deciphers the pivotal role of S. saprophyticus in mycotoxin-induced pulmonary fibrosis, highlighting the gut microbiota as a therapeutic target for preventing and treating mycotoxin-induced lung injury.

works.title: Discovery of Human Gut Bacteria Responsible for Biotransformation and Structural Diversification of Oat Steroidal Saponins
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Oat steroidal saponins undergo biotransformation by the gut microbiota, yet the bacteria involved and the structural diversity of the resulting metabolites remain incompletely characterized. Incubation of avenacoside B (AVE-B), a major oat steroidal saponin, with fecal microbiota from six human donors revealed marked interindividual variation in avenacoside E (AVE-E) production. Five bacterial species capable of AVE-B metabolism were isolated, with Bacteroides uniformis SS-F-0001 exhibiting the broadest metabolic profile. Quantitative PCR and carbohydrate-active enzyme profiling suggested that abundance alone did not explain conversion capacity. Comparative 1D and 2D NMR analysis of isolated AVE-E and its isomer revealed diagnostic C-22 and C-25 chemical-shift differences and H2-26 → C-22 HMBC correlations, supporting an isonuatigenin-type isomer with a six-membered F ring. These findings identify bacterial contributors to oat saponin metabolism and reveal structural diversity involving both deglycosylation and aglycone ring rearrangement, providing a basis for investigating the mechanisms and biological consequences of microbial saponin metabolism.

works.title: A Novel α2,3-Sialyltransferase Enabling the Synthesis of para α2,3-Sialylated Human Milk Oligosaccharides via Immobilized Cascade Enzymes
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Sialylated oligosaccharides are critical components of human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs). Rapid and efficient synthesis of these oligosaccharides is essential for investigating their functions and applications. In this study, a novel α2,3-sialyltransferase MsST was successfully identified through molecular docking and virtual screening. MsST was cascaded with CMP-sialic acid synthase to form a one-pot multienzyme system, which achieved a conversion rate exceeding 90% for various neutral core HMOs. Subsequently, the cascade enzymes were purified and immobilized in one step using nickel ferrite magnetic nanoparticles. The immobilized cascade enzymes retained 86% of their initial activity after 12 cycles and 70% at 37 °C after storage for 4 days, demonstrating high recyclability and storage stability. Therefore, seven sialylated HMOs, including three para α2,3-sialylated hexasaccharides, were synthesized from the neutral core HMOs in 91–96% recovery yields. This system provides an efficient platform for producing structurally defined α2,3-sialylated HMOs, facilitating the investigation of future functional food applications.

works.title: A Potential Probiotic Candidate Heyndrickxia ginsengihumi W1 is Associated with Increased Intestinal Stem Cell-Mediated Proliferation and Altered Barrier-Related Parameters: Potential Involvement of the Wnt/β-Catenin Pathway
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Probiotic properties of the rumen-derived strain Heyndrickxia ginsengihumi W1 were evaluated by whole-genome analysis, in vitro assays, and a short-term mouse model. Genome analysis preliminarily indicated no acquired antimicrobial resistance genes or virulence factors. In mice, W1 administration showed no obvious adverse effects under the present short-term experimental conditions, and was associated with Lactobacillus enrichment and elevated lactate in the jejunum. W1 administration was also associated with changes in selected jejunal barrier-related parameters and with increased intestinal stem cell (ISC)-mediated epithelial proliferation, potentially through the Wnt/β-catenin pathway. Jejunal lactate correlated positively with crypt depth, PCNA, ISC markers, and Wnt/β-catenin components. In vitro, purified lactate and W1 cell-free supernatant, but not heat-killed W1, promoted sheep intestinal epithelial cell proliferation, and lactate upregulated Axin2, Ctnnb1, and PCNA, but this lactate–Wnt/β-catenin mechanism remains a hypothesis requiring further validation. These results indicate that W1 may be a promising rumen-derived probiotic candidate.

Effect of film-forming solution pH on chitosan/cassava starch composite films loaded with purple sweet potato anthocyanins: Experiments, DFT calculations, and molecular dynamics studies
Understanding and modulating pea protein gelation: Molecular mechanisms, gel properties, and modification strategies
Beyond smell and taste: the role of mouthfeel in flavour perception and its implications for health and food innovation
works.abstract: Mouthfeel, encompassing the tactile, thermal, and chemesthetic sensations experienced during eating and drinking, is a crucial dimension of flavour perception. This review includes insights from sensory science, neurophysiology, biophysics, molecular biology, and food technology to provide a mechanistic perspective on mouthfeel and its relevance to nutrition and product development. We discuss how integrating this perspective with food design may enable better strategies to promote healthier and more satisfying diets.

works.title: Gelatin assisted RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a tandem assay for rapid detection of Listeria monocytogenes
works.abstract: Abstract Methods integrating isothermal amplification with the CRISPR/Cas12a system have gained significant attention due to their sensitivity and specificity. Herein, a gelatin-assisted recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA)-CRISPR/Cas12a tandem (GARC) assay was developed to detect Listeria monocytogenes . The GARC assay design exploited temperature-responsive gelatin to physically encapsulate CRISPR/Cas12a reagents, maintaining them in a gelled state during RPA incubation at 37 °C. This spatial separation prevents premature interaction between RPA and CRISPR components, while the gelatin at an appropriate concentration enhances fluorescence signal intensity, facilitating visual readout. The optimized GARC assay achieved a limit of detection (LOD) of 10 ag/μL for the hlyA gene, representing 10 4 and 10 7 fold improvements over paraffin-based one-pot RPA-CRISPR (100 fg/μL) and conventional PCR methods (100 pg/μL), respectively. Notably, the assay detected 8 CFU/mL of L. monocytogenes and 1.03 × 10 −5 ng/μL of genomic DNA, with favorable sensitivity (5/5) and specificity (16/16). Practical applicability was demonstrated through the successful detection of L. monocytogenes in salmon samples after 7-h enrichment at 20 CFU/25 g. This work introduces a versatile, visually interpretable platform with potential for food safety testing.

Selenized Sodium Alginate: Characterization and Its Effects on Muscle Nutritional Quality and Flavor Profile under High-Carbohydrate Challenge in Micropterus salmoides
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Sodium alginate was selenized via a BaCl2-catalyzed HNO3–Na2SeO3 method to produce selenized sodium alginate (Se-SA). Structural characterization confirmed covalent Se–O–C grafting, spherical nanoparticle formation (∼100 nm), and moderate depolymerization. A 12-week feeding trial with juvenile Micropterus salmoides (∼10 g) compared a high-carbohydrate diet (HC, 20%), HC + 1.0 mg/kg Na2SeO3 (HC-Se), HC + 1.0 mg/kg Se-SA (HC-Se-SA), and HC + 1.0 mg/kg sodium alginate (HC-SA). Dietary Se-SA significantly improved growth performance compared with other dietary treatments. Se-SA was associated with hepatic AMPKα activation and coordinate glycolipid gene regulation, correlating with reduced hepatic steatosis and improved glucose tolerance. Muscle n-3 PUFA content, texture, and antioxidant capacity were enhanced. HS-GC-IMS revealed remodeling of the volatile metabolome toward desirable aroma-active compounds and away from off-odors. These findings support Se-SA as a multifunctional polysaccharide additive for improving flesh quality in carbohydrate-intensive aquaculture.

works.title: Variations in the Deposition Behavior, Comprehensive Coloration Performance, and Storage Oxidative Stability of Different Carotenoids in Egg Yolk
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract The color of egg yolk has a significant impact on consumer acceptance, and its main coloring pigment comes from different carotenoids. This study evaluated the deposition and coloration capacity of dietary canthaxanthin, astaxanthin, and lutein in egg yolks, focusing on the oxidative stability of canthaxanthin. While physical parameters remained unaltered, canthaxanthin exhibited the highest coloration capacity, rapidly achieving a maximum color score of 16. Conversely, pigment mixtures yielded lower scores, suggesting visual dilution and competitive interactions, while LC–MS/MS revealed an upper limit on carotenoid deposition. Storage trials demonstrated that canthaxanthin-enriched yolks maintained exceptional color stability and chemical retention over 21 days at 4 °C and 15 °C. Notably, canthaxanthin maintained a consistently lower yolk pH throughout storage and attenuated superoxide dismutase (SOD) depletion. Precise single-pigment supplementation optimizes sensory quality and shelf life, providing practical strategies for laying hen feeding, egg processing, and retail industries.

works.title: ERRFI1 Deficiency Facilitates ErbB1 Hyperphosphorylation to Trigger NLRP3 Inflammasome-Mediated Pyroptosis in Arsenic-Induced Thyroid Injury: In Vivo and In Vitro Evidence
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Arsenicals are widespread endocrine-disrupting contaminants in agricultural environments and food supplies. Our prior work has linked arsenic exposure to thyroid cell pyroptosis and consequent tissue injury, yet the underlying molecular mechanism remains unclear. This study interrogated the ERRFI1-ErbB1/ERK axis mediating sodium arsenite (NaAsO2)-induced thyroid injury using in vivo SD rat models and in vitro Nthy-ori 3–1 cells. In rats, NaAsO2 decreased ERRFI1, boosted ErbB1/ERK phosphorylation, and caused thyroid injury and endocrine dysfunction; these adverse effects were partially reversed by the ErbB1 inhibitor erlotinib. In Nthy-ori 3–1 cells, NaAsO2 elicited NLRP3 inflammasome-dependent pyroptosis, repressed ERRFI1, hyperactivated ErbB1/ERK signaling. Pharmacological bidirectional modulation of ErbB1 confirmed its critical role, while ERRFI1 overexpression dampened ErbB1/ERK phosphorylation and mitigated pyroptosis. Collectively, NaAsO2 represses ERRFI1 to hyperactivate ErbB1/ERK, triggering NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated thyroid cell pyroptosis and endocrine dysfunction. These findings define a novel mechanism of arsenic thyrotoxicity and identify the ERRFI1-ErbB1/ERK axis as a promising intervention target.

works.title: Distinct Interaction Tendencies of Resveratrol and Chlorogenic Acid in Starch–Eicosapentaenoic Acid Systems and Their Relationships with Multiscale Structural Organization and Digestion Properties
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Amylose forms inclusion complexes with hydrophobic guests, but how additional bioactives regulate these assemblies through competitive or cooperative interactions remains unclear. Here, starch–unsaturated fatty acid–polyphenol ternary systems were constructed to investigate relationships among molecular interactions, multiscale structures, and digestion properties. Eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) was associated with V-type amylose ordering consistent with inclusion-complex formation, while the polyphenol-containing systems showed distinct patterns of structural organization. Resveratrol tended to associate with the hydrophobic helical environment, whereas chlorogenic acid showed stronger hydrogen-bond-mediated interaction tendencies around the starch–EPA assembly. Multiscale structural, digestion, and computational analyses revealed distinct associations between polyphenol interaction tendencies and digestion behavior. The RA-containing system showed lower digestibility, suggesting a contribution from structural restriction, whereas the CGA-containing system showed stronger α-amylase inhibition. These findings suggest that polyphenol structure shapes interaction patterns in starch–lipid assemblies and may inform future strategies for modulating starch structure and digestion properties.

works.title: Conformational and Rheological Changes of Hericium erinaceus Polysaccharides Driven by Molecular Weight Reduction and Their Impact on Prebiotic Effects
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Hericium erinaceus polysaccharide was degraded using microwave-assisted enzymatic hydrolysis to obtain four gradient molecular weight fractions (HePs). This study investigated the effects of molecular weight on their structural, rheological, and prebiotic properties. The reduction in molecular weight preserved the monosaccharide composition, functional groups, and residue types but significantly decreased their apparent viscosity and converted spatial conformations from compact and rigid triple-helix structures into flexible random coils. All HePs resisted in vitro gastrointestinal digestion and were utilized by gut microbiota. HePs increased the relative abundance of short-chain fatty acid-producing bacteria such as Megamonas, Megasphaera, Bifidobacterium, and Ligilactobacillus. The upregulation effects of HePs on the above intestinal microbiota and short-chain fatty acids were negatively correlated with molecular weight. Molecular weight may affect the modulatory effects of HePs on the dominant intestinal microbiota, functional enzyme expression, and microbial metabolic pathways. These findings may provide a research basis for the development of HePs prebiotic products.

works.title: Peptidomics Reveals That Goat Milk Is Closer to Human Milk Than Cow Milk in Proline-Rich Oligopeptide Release during In Vitro Dynamic Infant Digestion
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Human milk is the gold standard for infant nutrition. This study employed an in vitro dynamic infant gastrointestinal digestion model coupled with peptidomics to profile oligopeptide release from human, goat, and cow milk. Peptidomics identified 717, 658, and 514 oligopeptides from human, goat, and cow milk, respectively. Goat milk closely mirrored human milk in length distribution, with both peaking at 4–5 residues, whereas cow milk exhibited a peak at 6–7 residues. Proline was the most abundant amino acid residue across all sources, and goat milk generated significantly higher numbers of short oligopeptides (≤10 residues) than cow milk. Notably, 38 oligopeptides were exclusively shared between human and goat milk, predominantly proline-rich, casein-derived sequences with multiple predicted bioactivities. These findings indicate that goat milk is predicted to offer functional advantages over cow milk for human milk-oriented infant nutrition, primarily through its capacity to generate proline-rich bioactive oligopeptides.

works.title: Dietary Polystyrene Nanoplastics Exacerbate Valproate-Induced Hepatotoxicity via the Gut–Liver Axis, Involving Microbiota Dysbiosis and Metabolic Disorders
works.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
works.abstract: Abstract Nanoplastics (NPs) originating from plastic waste can enter crops and aquatic organisms, reaching the human body through dietary intake. This study investigated whether polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs) exacerbate valproate (VPA)-induced chemical liver injury via the gut–liver axis. Mice were exposed to VPA alone or in combination with PS-NPs for four consecutive weeks. Histopathological evaluation revealed more severe liver injury in the coexposure group compared to the VPA-alone group. Mechanistically, PS-NPs disrupted the gut microbiota and hepatic metabolic profiles, activated the NF-κB pathway, and inhibited the Nrf2 signaling pathway, collectively promoting inflammation, oxidative stress, and metabolic disorders. Intervention with mangiferin (MGF) alleviated these pathological changes. These findings suggest that PS-NPs, as emerging agricultural pollutants, aggravate chemical liver injury through an indirect mechanism mediated by the gut–liver axis.

A comprehensive review on mixed-culture fermentation for fruit wine: functional strains, microbial interaction mechanisms, quality regulation, influencing factors and future directions
works.journal: Critical Reviews in Food Science and Nutrition
works.abstract: Fruit wine fermentation involves a complex microbial ecosystem in which microbial metabolism and interspecies interactions collectively determine product quality. Although Saccharomyces cerevisiae-dominated fermentation ensures high efficiency and stability, its limited metabolic diversity restricts flavor complexity. Mixed-culture fermentation (MCF) has emerged as a promising strategy to improve fruit wine quality by leveraging the functional complementarity of diverse microorganisms. This review summarizes recent advances in MCF for fruit wine production, focusing on functional strains, mechanisms of microbial interaction, quality regulation, influencing factors, and industrial challenges. The roles of S. cerevisiae, non-Saccharomyces yeasts, lactic acid bacteria, and emerging microorganisms in regulating fermentation performance, aroma formation, organic acid balance, and the production of bioactive compounds are discussed. Furthermore, key interaction mechanisms are summarized, including nutrient competition, metabolite-mediated regulation, cell-to-cell contact, antagonism, and quorum sensing. These mechanisms collectively influence microbial succession and metabolic outcomes. Despite its potential for enhancing sensory complexity and functional properties, MCF faces challenges related to process controllability, strain commercialization, fermentation stability, and regulatory frameworks. Future studies should integrate multi-omics approaches and rational microbial consortium design to promote industrial application of MCF in fruit wine.

works.title: Electromagnetic- and irradiation-based technologies for microbial inactivation in solid foods: mechanisms, synergistic strategies, and future perspectives
works.journal: Critical Reviews in Food Science and Nutrition
works.abstract: Microbial control in solid foods is essential for ensuring safety and quality. Conventional thermal sterilization methods often lead to nutrient degradation, texture deterioration, and high energy consumption. As the food industry advances toward efficient processing, electromagnetic-based technologies-particularly non-thermal and multiphysics-coupled pasteurization approaches-have emerged as promising alternatives. This review explores the mechanisms, efficacy, and applicability of electromagnetic- and irradiation-based inactivation methods, including infrared, photothermal, microwave, radiofrequency, photodynamic, pulsed light, ultraviolet, and irradiation, in solid food matrices. These technologies offer potential for enhancing inactivation efficacy while better preserving food quality, yet challenges remain in addressing treatment uniformity, regulatory compliance, as well as process safety. Synergistic strategies that combine thermal and non‑thermal effects or integrate physical fields with antimicrobial agents demonstrate considerable promise for improving microbial control. However, widespread adoption faces obstacles, including high operational costs, and limited intelligent process control. Based on a synthesis of recent advances, this work outlines an integrated framework for food electromagnetic inactivation systems to highlight the need for further research in intelligent system design to advance the field.

works.abstract: Golden Flower Tibetan Tea polysaccharide components (GFTTPs) are polysaccharide-rich matrices generated during standardised “flowering” fermentation and may co-exist with tea pigments, phenolics and proteins. This study aimed to characterise GFTTPs and evaluate their metabolic effects in high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obese mice. GFTTPs were prepared by hot-water extraction, ethanol precipitation and dialysis, followed by compositional analysis and structural fingerprinting using FTIR, XRD, SEM, TGA/DTG and Py-GC/MS. GFTTPs exhibited an acidic, GalUA-rich composition with a medium-to-low molecular-weight distribution, predominantly amorphous organisation and an apparent porous morphology after freeze-drying. In vitro, GFTTPs showed concentration-dependent DPPH and ABTS radical-scavenging activities and FRAP reducing power, while α-glucosidase inhibition was modest compared with acarbose. In HFD-induced obese mice, 6-week administration of GFTTPs (600 mg kg −1 day −1 ) improved glucose tolerance and insulin responsiveness, reduced OGTT and IPITT AUCs, and improved fasting insulin-derived indices. GFTTPs also alleviated dyslipidaemia and transaminase elevation, accompanied by improved liver and pancreatic histopathology. Inflammatory and redox responses were partly restored, as shown by reduced TNF-α, increased IL-4, and recovered serum CAT and SOD activities, whereas IL-6 and MDA were less responsive. Microbiota and SCFA analyses indicated partial reversal of HFD-associated dysbiosis and SCFA remodelling, particularly increases in valerate and butyrate. Integrated correlation patterns suggested association-based links among gut microbiota, SCFAs and host metabolic phenotypes. Overall, GFTTPs provide a composition- and structure-characterised polysaccharide-rich tea-derived matrix with potential functional-food applications for metabolic health management.

Regulatory governance and full-scale digital transformation for prediction-based food safety management: Global trends and future perspectives
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Background The global food safety paradigm is shifting from traditional, reactive hazard control toward proactive, predictive risk management to address increasingly complex supply chain vulnerabilities. However, current digital implementations remain fragmented, creating structural bottlenecks that hinder the transition to next-generation regulatory science. Scope and approach To our knowledge, this study provides one of the first comparative critical analyses of the HACCP-based data governance frameworks of six major jurisdictions. We compare jurisdictions in which private actors play a relatively larger role in certification and implementation ('market-led': the United States, the European Union, Canada, and Japan) with those in which public institutions play a dominant role ('state-led': South Korea and China), positioned along a governance continuum in which all systems combine public and private functions, focusing on their capacity for real-time risk prediction, public-private data integration, and global interoperability. Key findings and conclusions The market-led systems examined tend to foster food safety culture but are affected by 'Data Silos' that limit actions to retrospective tracebacks. The state-led systems examined may enhance data integrity but can create a 'Data Island' paradox due to an over-reliance on automating isolated physico-chemical Critical Control Points. To overcome these limitations, we propose a conceptual framework for Full-Scale Digital Transformation (Full DX). Converging prerequisite programs, structured food safety culture assessment (e.g., Shapley-FAHP), and intentional threat mitigations (TACCP/VACCP) into an interoperable predictive network powered by ensemble machine learning could support a more resilient regulatory ecosystem for mitigating multidimensional global supply chain threats; this framework requires empirical validation.

works.title: The carcinogenic transition: toxicological, metabolic, and microbiome consequences of Westernized high-heat culinary practices in Asian populations
works.journal: Critical Reviews in Food Science and Nutrition
works.abstract: Colorectal and prostate cancer incidence has risen rapidly in several industrializing Asian populations. Dietary-pattern explanations focus on macronutrients, but cooking method is rarely examined. We discuss a “carcinogenic transition” hypothesis, in which a shift from moist-heat cooking (≤100 °C) toward dry-heat techniques (≥150 °C) increases formation of heterocyclic amines (HCAs) and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in food. We examine three components (the “Triple Threat” framework) that may be relevant to some populations: (1) dietary HCA/PAH exposure; (2) host variation in xenobiotic metabolism, including N-acetyltransferase 2 (NAT2), cytochrome P450 1A2 (CYP1A2), and aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (ALDH2) variants, which may alter bioactivation or clearance; and (3) diet-associated gut microbiome activity, including β-glucuronidase (GUS)-mediated deconjugation of excreted metabolites, supported by in vitro data with unquantified human magnitude. The framework rests on epidemiological associations and experimental mechanisms, not established causation. Confounding by obesity, alcohol, screening, and acculturation cannot be excluded, and trials isolating cooking method are needed. We also discuss practical food-preparation strategies, including lower-temperature cooking and antioxidant-rich marinades. Support comes from food-chemistry experiments and small urinary biomarker studies; effects on cancer incidence remain untested.
