Isoamyl isothiocyanate influences the oxidation-antioxidant homeostasis to maintain the postharvest quality of truffles (Tuber indicum)
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Truffles are highly susceptible to postharvest quality deterioration, primarily manifested as dehydration, microbial spoilage, and tissue softening. Isoamyl isothiocyanate (IAITC), as a volatile antimicrobial compound, exhibits multifaceted potential in the field of postharvest preservation of agricultural products. However, the effect of IAITC on postharvest truffles remains inconclusive. In this study, truffles were fumigated with 0, 5, 15, and 30 μL L -1 IAITC, and measured nutritional and quality indicators combined with the correlation analysis evaluation were conducted. Results showed that different concentrations of IAITC maintained nutrition, and retained sensory quality compared with the control group. Among the treatment groups, the 15 μL L -1 IAITC exhibited the best effect on improving postharvest fruit quality. At this concentration, IAITC maintained water content, and weight, inhibited bacterial growth and enhanced the activity of antioxidant enzymes (CAT and SOD). Concurrently, firmness, ASA, and soluble sugar (SS) were increased under 15 μL L -1 IAITC treatment. In addition, the pearson correlation analysis-PCA score plot indicated that different concentrations of IAITC had differential effects on postharvest of the truffles and that the effect at 15 μL was better. Collectively, IAITC treatment outcome followed the order 15 > 5 > 30 μL L -1 . These findings suggest that IAITC maintains the storage quality of truffles by simultaneously scavenging excess reactive oxygen species (ROS), maintaining redox homeostasis and suppressing microbial growth.

works.title: Effect of Different Yeast β-Glucan Addition Levels on the Structure, Functional Properties, and In Vitro Digestibility of Yak Myofibrillar Protein
works.abstract: Yak meat is a high-quality protein resource from the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, yet its high endogenous oxidative stress and inherently weak gel network under naturally low-fat conditions restrict processing quality improvement. This study investigated the dose-dependent effects of yeast β-glucan (YG, 0.5–2.5 g/dL) on yak myofibrillar protein (MP), with respect to oxidative status, structural properties, functional characteristics, gel performance and in vitro digestibility. A clear biphasic dose-response was observed: at dosages up to 1.5 g/dL, YG alleviated protein oxidation, maintained structural stability, and improved solubility, emulsifying capacity, gel quality and digestibility; in contrast, YG at 2.0 g/dL and above induced functional deterioration, coarsened gel microstructure and markedly decreased digestibility. The beneficial effects at moderate doses are proposed to relate to YG’s antioxidant activity and intermolecular interactions with MP, whereas high-dose deterioration may be associated with excessive steric hindrance and conformational disorder. Overall, 1.5 g/dL YG appears favorable for comprehensive performance under the tested conditions, providing a theoretical reference for the potential application of YG as a natural clean-label quality modifier in yak meat batter product development.

works.title: Isolation and characterization of three novel bacteriophages against pathogenic Escherichia coli and application in food
works.abstract: Pathogenic multidrug-resistant (MDR) Escherichia coli ( E. coli ) continues to threaten food safety and public health, and its increasing prevalence has made conventional prevention and control measures less reliable. In this study, three lytic E. coli bacteriophages (phages) with broad host range and strong antibacterial activity were isolated from fecal and wastewater samples collected from large-scale pig farms using pathogenic MDR E. coli as host bacteria. The three phages maintained infectivity across broad temperature and pH ranges and retained 81.60%–92.79% of their original titers under high-osmotic-pressure conditions. Treatment with ethanol, methanol, chloroform, or dimethyl sulfoxide reduced phage titers by 0.38 to 2.50 log 10 PFU/mL, indicating moderate tolerance to organic solvents. All three phages also markedly inhibited biofilm formation. Whole-genome analysis identified no antibiotic-resistance or virulence genes in any of the phage genomes, supporting their genetic safety for food-related applications. To evaluate their biocontrol potential, single phages and a three-phage cocktail were applied to raw pork, milk, and lettuce artificially contaminated with pathogenic MDR E. coli under simulated cold-chain storage and transportation (4°C) and ambient retail (25°C) conditions. Both single phages and the cocktail significantly lowered bacterial counts within 12 h, while the cocktail consistently produced stronger reductions than any single phage. After 24 h, compared with the untreated control, the phage cocktail reduced E. coli counts in raw pork, milk, and lettuce by 2.41-3.23 log 10 CFU/mL at 4°C and 2.24-3.49 log 10 CFU/mL at 25°C. These findings demonstrate that the three newly isolated phages, especially when combined as a cocktail, represent promising food-grade biocontrol candidates for improving the microbial safety of pork and other foods during storage, transport, and retail.

works.title: A comparative evaluation of six extraction methods on the techno-functional properties of black and white sesame meal proteins
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Sesame meal protein (SMP) is a promising sustainable protein source, yet its functional performance is often compromised by conventional extraction methods that prioritize yield over structural integrity. This study systematically compares six extraction methods-acid/alkaline pH-shift, Osborne fractionation, salting-out, isoelectric precipitation, and micellization-applied to black and white sesame varieties, aiming to establish a methodological reference for targeted SMP extraction. The extraction method critically dictated the supramolecular architecture and secondary structure of the isolates, which in turn governed their techno-functional properties. Micellization yielded isolates with superior pH-dependent solubility (exhibiting a pronounced U-shaped profile) and the highest in vitro digestibility (77.17% for black, 72.85% for white SMP); Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) observations suggested comparatively limited irreversible protein aggregation under micellization treatment. In contrast, isoelectric precipitation and pH-shift induced severe aggregation and unfolding, as evidenced by SEM and FTIR, leading to significantly impaired functionality. Osborne fractionation offered a viable yield-purity compromise, while salting-out achieved high purity with low recovery. Sesame variety was a key modulator, with black sesame yielding isolates of higher purity and distinct functional properties. These findings provide a practical reference for selecting extraction protocols to tailor SMP for specific food applications, such as protein-fortified beverages, nutritional emulsions, and texturized products.

works.title: Effects of Low Pressure Cold Plasma on the Structure and Techno-Functional Properties of Camel Milk Proteins
works.abstract: This study examined the dose‑dependent effects of atmospheric cold plasma (ACP) treatment on the structural, physicochemical, and techno‑functional properties of camel milk proteins (CMP). CMP samples were treated at 40–100 W for 10–20 min using a dielectric barrier discharge system. Initial screening across all conditions assessed solubility (pH 4.0–9.0), surface hydrophobicity, particle size, creaming stability, foaming property, antioxidant activity (DPPH/FRAP), degree of hydrolysis (DH), and FTIR spectroscopy. Moderate treatments improved solubility (up to 95% at pH 9.0), hydrophobicity, antioxidant capacity (79% DPPH scavenging), foaming (capacity 132%, stability 141%), and creaming stability (77%), due to protein unfolding and exposure of hydrophobic residues. Particle size decreased (minimum 383 nm) up to 15 min, indicating disaggregation, but prolonged exposure promoted aggregation, reduced solubility, and lowered DH (minimum 4%). FTIR revealed secondary structure changes, with increased β-sheet/random coil content and red-shifts in Amide I/II peaks. The 70 W/20 min condition was selected as optimal for balanced enhancements. Advanced analyses on this sample and control showed enhanced rheological properties (higher G’ modulus and yield stress), thermal stability (lower denaturation temperature, higher ΔH 0.51 J/g), and SDS-PAGE evidence of fragmentation/cross-linking. Overall, ACP offers a sustainable, non-thermal approach to optimize CMP for hypoallergenic food applications.

works.title: Importance of adequate sample preparation for the assessment of protein digestibility and quality
works.abstract: Determination of the nutritional quality of dietary proteins requires in vivo or in vitro digestion experiments that evaluate the ileal amino acid digestibility. However, many studies assess protein quality using finely ground flours or isolates rather than the food in its commonly consumed form, which may lead to overestimation of bioaccessibility. This study utilizes the standardized INFOGEST Quant protocol to evaluate the impact of sample preparation on protein digestibility and quality of chia and quinoa seeds, popularly known for their high protein quality. Total nitrogen, amino groups and individual amino acids were analyzed to calculate digestibility and digestible indispensable amino acid ratios (DIAAR). Results demonstrated that proteins in whole chia seeds, the most prevalent form of consumption, are virtually indigestible (< 4%), rendering their amino acids physiologically unavailable. Only upon grinding did chia’s protein digestibility surge to 63.3%, significantly increasing its DIAAR values and transforming it into a viable amino acid source. In contrast, quinoa exhibited high total protein digestibility (> 90%) upon both traditional processing (boiling) and grinding. These findings highlight that sample preparation is a determinant factor in protein quality assessment. To avoid overestimating the true nutritional value of plant-based “superfoods”, digestibility assays must mimic real-world consumption practices.

works.title: Insights into the effects of plasma-activated water process combined with low temperature on the storage quality of Boletus edulis: A multivariate analysis based on physicochemical property, HS-SPME-GC-MS and metabolomics
works.abstract: The postharvest quality deterioration of Boletus edulis limits its commercial value. This study innovatively investigates the effects of plasma-activated water (PAW) combined with low-temperature (4 °C) storage on its quality and flavor over 14 days, aiming to elucidate the underlying preservation mechanisms. Results showed that the combined treatment significantly retarded quality decline. Firmness decreased by only 34% (from 43.97 to 29.07 N), while malondialdehyde (MDA) content increased to 2.49 μmol/g, indicating that oxidative damage was well-regulated. Polyphenol oxidase (PPO) activity was markedly suppressed. A total of 59 volatile compounds, mainly consisting of esters and alcohols, were characterized by HS-SPME-GC-MS, and the variations in their contents were correlated with lipid oxidation. Untargeted metabolomics revealed that differential metabolites were mainly enriched in amino acid and lipid pathways, suggesting a potential anti-deterioration mechanism: PAW induced mild oxidative stress, activated antioxidant enzymes (e.g., POD), and modulated tryptophan (melatonin synthesis) and linoleic acid metabolism, thereby maintaining membrane stability and flavor balance. This work confirmed PAW combined with cold storage is a safe and effective strategy for Boletus edulis preservation. However, its impact on microbial community dynamics warrants further investigation.

works.title: Protein source and storage time influence the digestibility of caprylic and docosahexaenoic acids enriched plant-based oil-in-water emulsions
works.abstract: The physical and oxidative stability of oil-in-water emulsions, together with their digestibility, are critical parameters for their functionality and performance. However, although the effects of long-term storage on the stability of plant-protein-based emulsions are well documented, little is known about how it affects lipid digestion. This study thus aimed to determine the effect of 28-day mild storage on the bioaccessibility of caprylic acid (C8) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA; C22:6) in oil-in-water emulsions, using either pea protein isolate (PePI) or potato protein isolate (PoPI) as emulsifier. Throughout storage, both PePI and PoPI emulsions coalesced although the average droplet size of both emulsions remained <2 μm. PePI emulsions retarded the formation of primary lipid oxidation products compared to PoPI emulsions (3.7 versus 7.7 mmol/kg oil at the end of the storage). The bioaccessibility of C8 was higher for PePI emulsions (35-40 w/w %) compared to PoPI emulsions (15-25 w/w %) at the start of the intestinal digestion (p < 0.05). After storage, the bioaccessibility of C8 significantly decreased (p < 0.05). Digestibility should thus also be considered when determining the shelf-life of food products, especially if they are designed to promote health.

works.title: Construction and polygalacturonase-responsive behavior of whey protein-pectin nanocomposites prepared with pectins of different degrees of methoxylation
works.abstract: Protein-polysaccharide nanocomposites have emerged as promising carriers for stimuli-responsive delivery in intelligent food preservation. In this study, whey protein isolate (WPI) complexed with low-methylesterified pectin (LMP) or high-methylesterified pectin (HMP) was used to fabricate WPI/LMP (W-L-H) and WPI/HMP (W-H-H), respectively, via pH-induced electrostatic assembly. Polygalacturonase (PG) was employed as an enzymatic trigger. The results of molecular dynamics simulations showed that LMP exhibited stronger interactions with WPI, resulting in a lower binding energy (-79.78 kJ/mol) than that of W-H-H (-64.02 kJ/mol). After PG treatment, W-H-H exhibited higher PG responsiveness, accompanied by a greater increase in particle size than W-L-H. TEM and AFM results confirmed PG progressively disrupted the core-shell architecture, leading to particle aggregation. Furthermore, protein-pectin interactions were weakened, accompanied by protein conformational rearrangement and increased exposure of hydrophobic domains, with more pronounced changes observed in W-H-H. To verify the structure-responsiveness relationship at the emulsion level, thyme essential oil (TEO)-loaded emulsions stabilized by W-L-H (L-TEON) and W-H-H (H-TEON) showed encapsulation efficiencies above 95%. Compared with L-TEON, H-TEON underwent rapid droplet aggregation and coalescence following PG treatment. This study demonstrated the critical role of pectin methylation degree in regulating PG responsiveness, offering an effective strategy for precisely tuning active-agent release.

works.title: An enhanced methodology for the extraction of bioactive polysaccharides from Palmaria palmata
works.abstract: This study developed an efficient and environmentally friendly extraction method for obtaining multifunctional carbohydrate extracts from Palmaria palmata . Ethanol was applied for pigment removal, while citric acid (0.03 M) was selected as a safe, food-grade, and efficient extraction solvent. Among the evaluated techniques [solid-liquid extraction (SLE), ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE), and microwave-assisted extraction (MAE)], MAE yielded the highest total carbohydrate content (764.24 mg g -1 ) under optimized conditions (80 °C, 30 min, two cycles). Scanning electron microscopy analysis confirmed extensive cell wall disruption in MAE-treated samples, directly correlating with enhanced solute release. Comprehensive analytical characterization using complementary techniques such as Fourier Transform Infrared, Nuclear Magnetic Resonance, High Performance Size Exclusion Chromatography and Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry revealed a diverse carbohydrate profile, including a low-molecular-weight carbohydrate, tentatively identified as floridoside (α-D-galactopyranosyl-(1→2)-glycerol), and polysaccharides composed of xylose, galactose, and glucose. Additionally, the citric acid-assisted MAE extract exhibited strong tyrosinase inhibitory and antioxidant activities, supporting its multifunctional potential; HeLa cell viability remained above 70% at all concentrations of extract tested (0.5-10%), indicating no cytotoxic effects under the evaluated conditions. These findings highlight the potential of P. palmata MAE extract obtained with citric acid as green extraction solvent for applications in food preservation and nutraceutical formulations.

works.title: Co-fermentation of yeast and Lactobacillus plantarum improves noodle quality through protein-starch matrix reorganization in wheat quinoa semi-dried noodles
works.abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, using the non-fermented group as a control, the effects of yeast fermentation, Lactobacillus plantarum fermentation, and their co-fermentation were compared in protein fortified wheat quinoa semi-dried noodles. The effects of the different fermentation strategies on product qualities, protein-related structural characteristics, starch-related properties, and microstructure were evaluated. Compared with single-strain fermentation, co-fermentation reduced pH and cooking loss, significantly decreased chewiness ( P <0.05), and produced a more uniform color distribution, while maintaining excellent sensory quality. Co-fermentation was associated with increased free sulfhydryl content and reduced disulfide-bond contribution. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy showed decreased proportions of α-helix, β-sheet, and random coil, together with an increased proportion of β-turn, indicating changes in protein-related secondary structural characteristics. Fluorescence spectral changes further suggested partial unfolding of protein-related tertiary structure. These changes were accompanied by a more continuous protein phase observed in the noodle matrix. Co-fermentation also resulted in the highest relative crystallinity and set back value, and reduced the short-range order and enthalpy of the starch-related structure. Microscopic observations showed a more continuous protein distribution and a more open starch phase in co-fermentation noodles. Overall, co-fermentation established a distinct multiscale structure-quality profile relative to the two single-strain fermentation treatments, in which protein phase reorganization was accompanied by a selective redistribution of starch structure. These findings advance a matrix-level framework for interpreting how fermentation strategy is associated with coupled protein and starch structural evolution in complex cereal foods.

works.title: Unveiling β-carotene solubility behavior in subcritical water: Roles of temperature and Co-solvent from experiments and molecular insights
works.abstract: This study presents a novel combined experimental and molecular simulation approach to unravel the mechanisms underlying the enhanced solubility of β-carotene, a key bioactive compound, in subcritical water (368.15–408.15 K, 5 MPa) using ethanol (0–10% wt/wt) as a cosolvent. Experimental results demonstrated a pronounced increase in β-carotene solubility with temperature and ethanol concentration, with the addition of 10% ethanol at 368.15 K increasing solubility by 95%. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, applied for the first time to this system, accurately reproduced these trends and provided molecular-level insights. Structural analyses revealed that ethanol acts as an active cosolvent and molecular bridge, leveraging its polar hydroxyl group and nonpolar ethyl moiety to reduce solvent polarity while facilitating solute–solvent interactions. Dynamic analyses showed that at 388.15 K, 10% ethanol increased the diffusion coefficient of β-carotene by ∼80%, highlighting the synergistic effect of enhanced structural compatibility and molecular mobility on solubility. By bridging macroscopic solubility measurements with microscopic structural and dynamic understanding, this work establishes a framework for designing efficient green solvent systems. The findings guide optimizing extraction, formulation, and processing of poorly soluble bioactive compounds, offering a pathway toward environmentally friendly and highly effective solubilization strategies.

works.title: Plasma-assisted annealing of corn starch: Influence of dry and aqueous dielectric barrier discharge plasma pretreatments on structure and physicochemical properties
works.abstract: : This study investigated the effects of dry and wet dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) plasma pretreatments, alone or combined with annealing, on the multi-scale structure and functional properties of corn starch. Plasma treatments caused no obvious granule fragmentation, but altered surface morphology, particle size distribution, and crystalline organization. Dry plasma mainly induced surface etching and increased specific surface area, whereas wet plasma produced a distinct modification pattern with limited surface erosion. Both plasma treatments reduced relative crystallinity, while annealing promoted molecular rearrangement and improved crystalline perfection. FT-IR and DSC results showed that plasma-assisted annealing enhanced short-range molecular order and thermal stability, with wet plasma-assisted annealing (WP-ANN) exhibiting the highest onset gelatinization temperature and enthalpy. In addition, plasma and annealing significantly affected hydration, pasting, rheological, and digestibility properties. Dry plasma increased paste development and enzymatic susceptibility, whereas wet plasma reduced swelling and pasting viscosity but improved thermal resistance. Notably, WP-ANN showed the highest paste transparency, the lowest rapidly digestible starch content, and the highest resistant starch content. These findings demonstrate that DBD plasma can serve as an effective pretreatment to tailor starch structure during annealing, and that the treatment medium plays a decisive role in determining the final structure-function relationship.

works.title: pH-dependent modulation of gelation and digestive properties of pork myofibrillar protein by tea polyphenol-loaded ternary nanoparticles for safe swallowing in dysphagia management
works.abstract: The growing prevalence of dysphagia demands texture-modified foods that reconcile swallowing safety with nutritional functionality. To address this structure–function paradox, we designed a pH-responsive, multilayered hydrocolloid network that reinforces gel mechanics while modulating digestion. Ternary nanoparticles were assembled layer-by-layer via electrostatic deposition of anionic sodium alginate (SA) and cationic quaternary ammonium chitosan (QAC) onto a tea polyphenol (TP)-loaded Flammulina velutipes protein (FVP) core, yielding optimal colloidal properties (364.6 nm; encapsulation efficiency >80%) and enhanced interfacial activity. Across pH 5–9, weakly alkaline conditions (pH 8–9) promoted a dense myofibrillar protein (MP) gel network stabilized by synergistic hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic interactions, and dynamically regulated disulfide bonds, with β-sheet and β-turn contents totaling 71.9%, storage modulus >1600 Pa, and improved thermal stability. The gels met IDDSI Level 6 criteria and showed high sensory acceptability. This dense architecture acted as a pH-dependent gatekeeper: a physical barrier at gastric pH 2.0 that delayed premature proteolysis, yet fully disintegrated at intestinal pH 7.5, achieving 93.7% protein digestibility with sustained TP release. These results demonstrate that a rationally designed polysaccharide–protein interpenetrating network can decouple mechanical strength from digestibility, offering a versatile platform for dysphagia-targeted foods that integrate swallowing safety with programmed nutrient release and meet older adults' dual needs of aspiration-risk mitigation and adequate nutrition.

works.title: Sonicated black chickpea aquafaba as a sustainable egg-white substitute in sponge cakes
works.abstract: The food industry's heavy reliance on animal proteins, particularly egg white, has raised significant environmental and ethical concerns, while the resource-intensive nature of livestock production and the growing demand for vegan products underscore the urgent need for sustainable plant-based alternatives. Aquafaba, the liquid by-product of legume cooking, has emerged as a promising functional ingredient; however, its application as an egg-white replacer—especially from black chickpea and through ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE)—remains underexplored. This study investigated the application of ultrasound-assisted extracted (UAE) black chickpea aquafaba as a functional replacer for egg white in sponge cakes. The aquafaba was incorporated at five substitution levels (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%). Physicochemical, textural, and sensory properties were comprehensively analyzed. Results indicated that UAE improved the thermal stability of aquafaba without chemical alteration. In cakes, higher aquafaba levels significantly increased moisture content and specific volume (e.g., a 69% rise at 100% substitution) but markedly decreased textural parameters such as hardness (41% reduction at 75%). Sensory evaluation revealed that cakes with up to 50% aquafaba maintained acceptable flavor, mouthfeel, and overall liking, comparable to the control. Beyond 50%, sensory quality, particularly color and texture, declined. The study concludes that a 50% substitution level is optimal, demonstrating the potential of black chickpea aquafaba as a sustainable, plant-based ingredient for developing cost-effective and high-quality plant-based baked goods.

works.title: Preliminary screening of candidate aroma compounds associated with “Wok Hei” and characterization of “Wok Hei” formation-dissipation patterns during stir-frying and post-cooking standing
works.abstract: : This study used cauliflower as a uniform stir-frying matrix to explore the chemical composition and formation-dissipation characteristics of “Wok Hei” in traditional Chinese stir-fried dishes. Experimental groups with varied condiment formulations were prepared. Sensory evaluation, gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS), gas chromatography-olfactometry (GC-O), and partial least squares regression (PLSR) combined with relative odor activity value (ROAV) were used to screen aroma-active volatiles closely associated with “Wok Hei”. Gas chromatography-ion mobility spectrometry (GC-IMS) was used to monitor dynamic volatile variations during stir-frying and post-cooking standing. The sensory profile of “Wok Hei” was characterized by seven core sensory attributes: savory, soy sauce-like, scalliony, garlicky, roasty, fatty, and slightly burnt. In total, 45 volatiles were detected using GC-MS, and 52 volatile features (39 annotated) were detected using GC-IMS. Multivariate statistics combined with ROAV analysis screened 11 aroma-active compounds as candidate contributors to “Wok Hei”, mainly including aldehydes, sulfur-containing compounds, and heterocycles. Analysis of formation and dissipation patterns in the fully seasoned lard-containing group, which showed the strongest “Wok Hei” sensory intensity, indicated that the duration from soy sauce addition to the end of stir-frying corresponded to the primary formation window of “Wok Hei”, whereas the first 10 min of post-cooking standing constituted the predominant dissipation phase. Three additional stage-discriminating volatile markers were further screened from GC-IMS profiles. These candidate “Wok Hei”-related volatiles detected using both platforms showed obvious dissipation within this 10-min post-cooking standing period. This study offers baseline information for flavor reconstruction and quality control of “Wok Hei” in industrialized Chinese stir-fried cuisine.

works.title: Development and performance evaluation of a pressure-driven gastric simulation system for tofu disintegration and protein digestion
works.abstract: Food structure plays a critical role in determining digestion behavior by influencing mechanical breakdown and nutrient release during gastric digestion. This study investigated the effects of gastric mechanical forces on the structural disintegration and protein digestion of tofu using a pressure-driven Korea Food Research Institute (KFRI) gastric simulation system (KGSS). The KGSS employs hydraulic actuation to generate cyclic compression and expansion, enabling the controlled simulation of gastric mechanical conditions. Its performance was evaluated using tofu as a model food and compared with that of a static digestion model and a commercial gastric digestion simulator (GDS). Both dynamic systems promoted greater structural disintegration than the static model. Quantitative analyses showed similar patterns of solid fraction redistribution and particle size reduction between the KGSS and GDS. At 3 h of digestion, particle sizes were 30.40 μm in the KGSS and 28.79 μm in the GDS, compared with 39.74 μm in the static model. Despite similar structural breakdown, protein release differed between the dynamic systems, reaching 5.61 ± 0.09 g/L in the KGSS and 6.87 ± 0.09 g/L in the GDS at 3 h. SDS-PAGE analysis further showed differences in protein band profiles between the KGSS and GDS, which may reflect both protein release and enzymatic degradation. These findings demonstrate that gastric mechanical conditions influence food structural breakdown and protein digestion and highlight the applicability of the KGSS as a controllable platform for investigating digestion behavior under defined mechanical conditions.

works.title: Technological effects and prebiotic potential of microcrystalline cellulose and hydrolyzed nanocrystalline cellulose in low-fat and non-fat probiotic yogurt
works.abstract: This study investigated the effects of microcrystalline cellulose (MCC) and hydrolyzed nanocrystalline cellulose (HCNC) on the technological properties of non-fat (NF) and low-fat (LF) set yogurts, alongside their in vitro potential to support the growth of selected probiotic strains. The physicochemical properties of MCC and HCNC were characterized, revealing fibrous structures via field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM) and distinct viscosities (3989.33 vs. 910.29 mPa·s). Prebiotic potential was evaluated using Lactobacillus casei and Bifidobacterium longum , where both compounds exhibited superior growth-promoting activity compared to cellulose and comparable efficacy to inulin. Six yogurt treatments (NF/LF with MCC, HCNC, or control) were evaluated for physicochemical, microbiological, and sensory properties over a 24-day storage period at 4 ± 1 °C. Results indicated that MCC and HCNC significantly improved textural firmness, apparent viscosity, and water-holding capacity while effectively reducing syneresis in both NF and LF matrices (P < 0.05). Although titratable acidity increased and pH decreased during storage, the structural integrity remained intact, with a cohesive network and minimal porosity, as confirmed by FE-SEM. Notably, MCC and HCNC supplementation significantly increased probiotic viability compared with controls, with final counts exceeding recommended levels (up to 7.43 log CFU·g -1 ). Sensory evaluation revealed that low-fat samples were preferred over non-fat yogurts; additionally, samples containing MCC or HCNC received higher scores for mouthfeel, texture consistency, and overall acceptance, along with lower perceived whey separation, than the control samples. Overall, MCC and HCNC show potential as multifunctional ingredients to modify selected technological properties and support probiotic viability in low-fat and non-fat yogurt, although their ability to replace the functions of milk fat requires further validation against a full-fat reference formulation.

works.title: Whole-genome sequencing-guided development of a strain-specific quantitative PCR assay for monitoring Bacillus velezensis NY12-2 during Korean soybean fermentations
works.abstract: This study developed a strain-specific quantitative PCR (qPCR) assay for Bacillus velezensis NY12-2, a functional starter strain used in Korean soybean fermentation. Accurate strain-level identification is essential because culture-dependent methods cannot reliably distinguish B. velezensis NY12-2 from closely related Bacillus strains in complex fermentation matrices. Using whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and BLAST-based comparative analysis, we identified strain-specific genomic regions and designed highly specific primers. The assay consistently detected B. velezensis NY12-2 in inoculated samples and showed reliable standard curve performance for quantitative analysis. Matrix interference initially caused discrepancies between qPCR-based and plate count-based quantification, with mean deviations of 1.15 log CFU/g in cheonggukjang and 1.39 log CFU/g in meju . A regression-based correction model reduced these deviations to 0.16 log CFU/g and 0.56 log CFU/g, respectively, improving quantitative precision. The assay also maintained specificity and reproducible performance under co-culture conditions with Aspergillus oryzae , which reflects the mold-associated microbial environment of Korean soybean fermentation. Overall, this qPCR assay provides a reliable molecular tool for strain-level monitoring and traceability of B. velezensis NY12-2 and may support process optimization, quality control, and starter culture management in soybean-based fermentation.

works.title: Effects of different pretreatments on the quality of walnut oil bodies
works.abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigated the effects of three thermal pretreatments—microwave heating, roasting, and steaming—on walnut raw materials, followed by aqueous extraction of oil bodies (OBs). The physicochemical properties of walnut oil bodies (WOBs) were analyzed, including particle size, confocal laser scanning microscopy observations, water distribution, and gel electrophoresis, with underlying mechanisms discussed. The results demonstrated that different pretreatments significantly influenced the extracted OBs. Compared to the control group, the microwave-treated group exhibited the smallest particle size, which was consistent with CLSM results showing more uniform oil droplet distribution. Analysis of water distribution and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) imaging revealed that microwave treatment at 210 W yielded the optimal overall performance, with the tightest binding between water and OBs, as well as the most stable OBs structure. WOBs hold broad application potential in the food industry. This study not only expands their utilization prospects but also provides critical theoretical support for their future food applications.

works.title: Enhanced thermal stability, antioxidant activity, and in vitro release behaviour of curcumin in superfine grinding-based pea protein–chitosan nanoparticles via multi-scale structure-function mapping
works.abstract: : Protein–polysaccharide nanoparticles represent promising carriers for functional food ingredients, yet the influence of protein conformation on their co-assembly and functional performance has remained insufficiently characterised. To validate the hypothesis that nanoparticles formed through co-assembly of pea protein isolate (PPI) and chitosan (CS) may be regulated by protein molecular conformation, this study employed superfine grinding as a chemical-free, food-grade physical modification strategy that enables time-dependent and controllable conformational tuning of PPI to obtain superfine grinding-modified PPI (sPPI), then prepared curcumin-loaded composite nanoparticles via self-assembly. The objective of this study was to characterise superfine grinding-induced PPI conformational changes, evaluate their impact on PPI-CS nanoparticle assembly and properties, and assess curcumin loading, antioxidant activity, and gastrointestinal release behaviour. Compared to the unmodified PPI-CS system, the sPPI-6-CUR-CS formulation achieved the highest encapsulation efficiency of 92.08% and drug loading capacity of 9.44%. The sPPI-4-CS formulation exhibited the highest three-phase contact angle at 80.6°. The sPPI-8-CS formulation reached the highest thermal denaturation temperature of 84.85°C, providing optimal thermal protection for heat-sensitive encapsulated compounds. Furthermore, sPPI-CUR-CS released curcumin more gradually in simulated gastric fluid (SGF) and more rapidly in simulated intestinal fluid (SIF) than PPI-CUR-CS, with cumulative gastric release as low as 1.78% and total intestinal release reaching 48.65%.In conclusion, time-dependent modification of PPI conformation through superfine grinding significantly enhances the thermal stability, loading capacity, antioxidant properties, and delivery performance of composite nanoparticles, providing a theoretical basis for targeted nanoparticle design and development of functional food products.

works.title: Calix[4]arene-based Cd(Ⅱ) coordination polymer/reduced graphene oxide composite for sensitive electrochemical sensing of protocatechuic acid in fruits
works.abstract: Herein, a calix[4]arene-based Cd(II) coordination polymer (Cd-L) was synthesized by the solvothermal method. Subsequently, a series of Cd-L/RGO-x composites was prepared by integrating Cd-L with reduced graphene oxide (RGO). Electrochemical measurements indicated that the glassy carbon electrode modified with Cd-L/RGO-2 (Cd-L/RGO-2/GCE) showed the most outstanding electrocatalytic properties toward protocatechuic acid (PCA) due to the synergistic effects between Cd-L and RGO. Cd-L offers plentiful catalytic sites and specific adsorption capacity for PCA via hydrogen bonding, while RGO forms an efficient conductive network to promote interfacial electron transfer. The Cd-L/RGO-2/GCE sensor featured an extremely low detection limit of 35 nmol/L for PCA in the linear ranges of 0.02–200 μmol/L. Importantly, the Cd-L/RGO-2/GCE sensor was applied to analyze the content of PCA in actual pear and red plum samples, obtaining favorable spike recoveries (95.80%–103.70%). This work develops a reliable tool for the sensitive detection of trace PCA in fruit matrices.

works.title: Mass spectrometry imaging reveals the metabolic geography underlying spatial programming of necrotrophic infection in postharvest sweet cherry
works.abstract: Brown rot, caused by Monilinia spp., is a destructive postharvest disease of cherry. This study employed MALDI-MSI to decipher metabolic interaction networks during four infection stages: 0 h (T0), 24 h (T1), 48 h (T2), and 96 h (T3). Eight key differential metabolites, selected based on combined statistical criteria (VIP > 1.0 from cross-validated PLS-DA, univariate p < 0.05, and q < 0.05 after Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction), were identified and assigned putative origins (host- or pathogen-derived) based on literature-reported biosynthetic pathways and comparative spatial distribution against uninfected controls, covering fungal toxins, host defenses, cell wall components, and energy markers. Temporal analysis revealed a three-stage pathogenic strategy: T0–T1 colonization, potentially characterized by elevated flavonoid (aurone) signals at the infection front followed by apparent oxidative degradation, coinciding with itaconic acid accumulation potentially consistent with metabolic immune responses; T1–T2 expansion, with reduced 4-hydroxyproline-rich cell wall signals and declining phenolic defense (caffeoylmalic acid) at the infection front, a pattern suggestive of enzymatic attack; T2–T3 necrosis, featuring accumulation of putative fungal toxins and lipid hydrolysis products (e.g., arachidyl alcohol) in the necrotic core alongside diminished host energy metabolites, potentially consistent with ROS-associated cell death and nutrient scavenging. Spatially, the infection front (2–5 mm) accumulated defense metabolites, while the necrotic core enriched toxins. The dynamics of host defense metabolites (itaconic acid and β-nicotinate d-ribonucleotide), which peaked at T1 and subsequently declined, suggest 24 h as a putative critical defense window. This study provides a novel framework for understanding necrotrophic infection and informs postharvest preservation strategies.

works.title: Effects of atmospheric cold plasma and ultrasound pre-treatments of whey protein on the physicochemical and functional properties of spray-dried whey protein powder
works.abstract: The production of spray-dried whey protein powders with high functional performance remains challenging because thermal stress during spray drying promote protein denaturation and aggregation, thereby reducing their techno-functional properties. Although atmospheric cold plasma (ACP) and ultrasound (US) have each been reported to improve whey protein functionality, information regarding their sequential application before spray drying remains limited. Therefore, this study investigated both the individual and combined effects of ACP (20 kV, 3 and 6 min) and US (600 W, 10 and 30 min) pretreatments on the physicochemical, structural, and functional properties of spray-dried whey protein powder. Sequential ACP–US pretreatment markedly enhanced powder functionality compared with the untreated control and the individual treatments. The CP6–US30 treatment exhibited the highest protein solubility (93.1%), oil absorption capacity (1.72 mL g -1 ), foaming capacity (87.1%), and emulsifying activity, while also reducing hydrodynamic aggregate size and improving wettability and dispersibility. This study demonstrates for the first time, the effectiveness of sequential ACP–US pretreatment prior to spray drying for improving the functional quality of whey protein powder. The findings provide a promising non-thermal strategy for producing high-performance whey protein ingredients suitable for instant beverages, dairy products, and other protein-enriched food formulations.

works.title: Wine processing remodels the metabolome and enhances antioxidant activity of rhubarb: Insights from flavor analysis and feature-based molecular networking
works.abstract: Wine processing is a traditional technique applied to rhubarb to enhance its functional properties; however, the underlying chemical transformation mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, an integrated strategy combining response surface methodology, ultra-fast gas chromatography electronic nose (GC E-nose), untargeted metabolomics, and feature-based molecular networking (FBMN) was established to systematically investigate the processing-induced chemical transformation of wine-processed rhubarb (WPR). A multi-dimensional quality evaluation system based on physicochemical and antioxidant indicators was first constructed to optimize the processing parameters. Compared with raw rhubarb (RR), WPR exhibited significantly enhanced antioxidant activity, accompanied by increased contents of total phenolics, total flavonoids, and free anthraquinones. Colorimetric analysis further revealed pronounced darkening and desaturation after processing. Volatile profiling identified 28 aroma-related compounds, and multivariate analysis demonstrated substantial remodeling of the volatile composition during wine processing. Metabolomics combined with FBMN annotated 334 metabolites and revealed extensive transformation of anthraquinones, and phenolics. In particular, structurally complex anthraquinone derivatives were likely transformed into smaller free aglycones and low-molecular-weight phenolics. The observed metabolic patterns and MS/MS fragmentation characteristics were consistent with hydrolysis, bond cleavage, oxidation, and depolymerization processes during wine processing. Multi-dimensional correlation analysis further demonstrated close associations among volatile variation, chemical remodeling, color alteration, and antioxidant enhancement. Overall, this study provides new insights into the processing-induced chemical transformation mechanisms of rhubarb and offers a comprehensive analytical framework for investigating functional food processing.

works.title: Cold Plasma Modulates Microbial Community Structure, Enhances Quality Attributes and Extends Shelf Life of Chilled Mutton
works.abstract: Chilled mutton is highly nutritious; however, oxidation and microbial contamination during refrigerated storage can lead to quality deterioration, safety risks, and economic losses. Cold plasma (CP), an emerging nonthermal preservation technology, has considerable potential for controlling microbial contamination in food. This study evaluated the effects of CP treatment on the quality of chilled mutton stored at 4 °C for 30 days. Changes in bacterial communities and metabolite profiles were further characterized using 16S rRNA sequencing and non-targeted metabolomics. On day 30, CP treatment reduced the total viable count (TVC) and Pseudomonas population by 1.25 and 2.5 log CFU/g, respectively. Sequencing analysis also revealed that Carnobacterium became the predominant genus instead of Pseudomonas . Moreover, CP treatment delayed the deterioration of meat color and sensory properties and limited the increases in pH, thiobarbituric acid-reactive substances (TBARs), and total volatile basic nitrogen (TVB-N) during storage ( P < 0.05), thereby prolonging the shelf life of chilled mutton. Non-targeted metabolomic analysis revealed lower relative histamine abundance in CP-treated samples. Overall, CP treatment maintained the quality and extended the storage life of chilled mutton by reshaping the microbial community structure, supporting its potential application as a nonthermal preservation strategy.

works.title: Nutritionally enhanced plant-based gluten-free cookies from green banana-rice-mung bean composite flour enriched with Wolffia globosa
works.abstract: Developing plant-based, gluten-free (GF) bakery products remains challenging due to gluten absence and refined starch nutritional limitations. This study evaluated Wolffia globosa powder (WP; 0-65% w/w, flour basis) fortification in GF cookies formulated on a green banana-rice-mung bean composite flour. A lower-protein composite flour system (Premix A) yielded a significantly higher ( p < 0.05) water absorption index and swelling power, supporting baking matrix expansion. Dough firmness increased significantly ( p < 0.05) at ≥ 39% WP via protein-fiber water competition and particle filling. In baked cookies, ≥ 13% WP significantly elevated ( p < 0.05) ash, total phenolic content, and 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) radical scavenging activity, whereas protein enrichment required ≥ 26% WP ( p < 0.05). All formulations maintained complete essential amino acid and essential fatty acid profiles. Microstructurally, matrices remained continuous at 13-26% WP, whereas inclusions ≥ 52% induced micro-cavities and volatile off-flavors. Consequently, 13% WP was identified as the optimal threshold, achieving bioactive enrichment while preserving structural integrity and sensory acceptance. These findings establish W. globosa as a viable ingredient for GF fortification, warranting future studies on digestibility kinetics, glycemic index, and shelf-life stability.

works.title: Tracking endogenous lipids and other non-protein components upon dry or wet fractionation of faba bean flour
works.abstract: Protein fractionation is widely used to produce protein-rich ingredients; however, the effects of the fractionation pathway on the fate of non-protein components remain poorly understood. Here, faba bean flour (FFL) from a single cultivar was processed to a protein concentrate (FPC) by dry fractionation and a protein isolate (FPI) by wet fractionation. As expected, both fractionation routes increased the protein content from 295 in FFL to 580 and 809 g/kg DM in FPC and FPI, respectively. Endogenous lipids were found to accumulate upon fractionation, reaching 75 g/kg in FPI. Lipids in FPI had very low extractability in hexane compared to those in FFL and FPC. Confocal microscopy showed the colocalisation of lipids with protein aggregates in FPI, suggesting that wet fractionation induced a profound reorganisation of the endogenous lipid fraction through the formation of lipid-protein co-assemblies. Their presence may contribute to the lower aqueous solubility of proteins in FPI (641 g/kg protein) compared to FPC (839 g/kg protein). Phytic acid and polyphenols were effectively removed from FPI, but were concentrated in FPC. Taken together, these findings confirm that the fractionation route determines not only the ingredients’ detailed composition but also the structural organisation of proteins with minor components, which may have consequences for ingredient functionality. The trade-off between protein purity, presence of secondary metabolites, and functionality should be carefully considered depending on the intended application.

works.title: Development, Characterization, and Storage Stability of Freeze-Dried Bottle Gourd (Lagenaria siceraria) Juice Powder from Enzyme-Assisted Extracted Juice
works.abstract: This study developed and characterized freeze-dried bottle gourd juice powder from juice extracted with pectinase and cellulase (EBGJP), compared it with a control powder (BGJP) made without enzymes, and evaluated its storage stability at 10 and 30 °C for 90 days. Enzymatic extraction increased juice yield from 54.3% to 80.09% and DPPH activity from 52.1% to 84.04% (p < 0.05). Compared with BGJP, EBGJP had higher powder recovery (10.62 vs 7.85%), lower water activity (0.22 vs 0.31), higher solubility (95.72 vs 89.34%) and shorter reconstitution time (42.18 vs 56.21 s) (p < 0.001). After 90 days at 30 °C vs 10 °C, moisture (7.91 vs 5.82%), Thiobarbituric acid (TBA) value (1.46 vs 0.65 mg MDA/kg) and Hydroxymethyl furfural (HMF) were higher, and Total phenol content (TPC) and DPPH activity lower (p < 0.01). Chilled storage with moisture-barrier packaging is recommended for this nutrient-concentrated powder. Pectinase and cellulase-assisted extraction increased juice recovery and promoted the release of soluble solids and bioactive substances before freeze-drying. The obtained powder had a low moisture content, good functional characteristics, and a porous amorphous microstructure suitable for reconstitution. Processing significantly affected the physicochemical and antioxidant properties of bottle gourd juice. Storage experiments showed that refrigeration was superior to ambient storage in maintaining the quality of the product, as higher temperatures increased moisture uptake, lipid oxidation, non-enzymatic browning, and microbiological development. The results showed that antioxidant activity and bioactive substances decreased during storage, with accelerated losses under ambient settings. Overall, enzyme-assisted extraction followed by freeze-drying resulted in a nutrient-concentrated powder with good functional properties; during 90 days of storage in LDPE pouches, quality loss was markedly greater at 30 °C than at 10 °C.

works.title: Characterization of flaxseed oil microcapsules: Fabrication with flaxseed protein-gum conjugates as wall materials
works.abstract: To enhance the oxidative stability of flaxseed oil (FO), flaxseed protein isolate (FPI) and its covalent conjugates with flaxseed gum (FG) were employed as wall materials to fabricate FO microcapsules. Relative to neat FPI microcapsules (FPI-FO-M), microcapsules fabricated from FPI-FG conjugates (FPI-FG-FO-M) possessed better antioxidative stability, owing to covalent crosslinking between FPI and FG. Results showed that FPI-FG-FO-M achieved a higher encapsulation efficiency (EE) of 89.75 ± 1.14% and a smaller average particle size (20.58 ± 0.14 μm). Structural characterizations verified successful encapsulation, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) observations indicated that both microcapsule groups retained intact spherical shapes. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) demonstrated that FPI-FG-FO-M possessed outstanding thermal stability, while microencapsulation did not change the fatty acid (FA) profile of FO. Under low-temperature, dark, and anaerobic storage environments, the oil retention rates of FPI-FG-FO-M reached 96.32%, 96.39%, and 96.20%, respectively. Accelerated oxidation trials revealed that the percentage increase in peroxide value (POV) for FPI-FG-FO-M was only 12.40%, far below the 26.36% measured for FPI-FO-M; the oxidation kinetics conformed to a first-order kinetic model. At 25 °C, microencapsulation effectively enhanced the storage stability of FO. The shelf lives of FPI-FO-M and FPI-FG-FO-M were 1.63-fold and 1.90-fold those of non-encapsulated FO, respectively. During simulated gastrointestinal digestion, FPI-FG-FO-M displayed a lower final release of free fatty acids and higher retention of α-linolenic acid (C18:3, 56.38 ± 0.25%). In conclusion, covalent conjugates derived from whole flaxseed processing by-products represent ideal and sustainable wall materials for the microencapsulation of oxidation-susceptible plant oils.

works.title: Tea polyphenols accelerate conjugative transfer of antibiotic resistance plasmids via metabolic reprogramming-driven hydroxyl radical generation
works.abstract: Tea polyphenols (TPP) are widely used in tea beverages, functional foods, dietary supplements, and food-related products because of their antioxidant and antimicrobial properties. However, their potential influence on the dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) remains largely unclear. In this study, we found that sub-inhibitory concentrations of TPP significantly promoted the conjugative transfer of multiple antibiotic resistance plasmids both within and across bacterial species. Mechanistically, TPP induced metabolic perturbations characterized by enhanced tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle activity and respiratory metabolism, which were accompanied by excessive intracellular ROS accumulation, particularly hydroxyl radical generation. Disruption of iron-sulfur clusters and subsequent Fe 2+ -dependent Fenton reaction further amplified oxidative stress, thereby facilitating plasmid transfer. Deletion of the malate dehydrogenase (MDH) gene markedly reduced ROS production and abolished the promotive effect of TPP on conjugation, highlighting an important role of metabolic remodeling in this process. In addition, TPP increased bacterial membrane permeability and altered the transcription of conjugation-associated genes, including repression of global regulatory genes and activation of genes involved in mating pair formation and DNA transfer. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that TPP can facilitate plasmid-mediated ARG dissemination through coordinated metabolic and oxidative mechanisms, highlighting a potential food safety concern associated with natural bioactive compounds.
