works.title: Effects of substrate and salt concentration on quality attributes of alternative legume-based misos during long-term fermentation
works.abstract: The long-term evolution of quality attributes in alternative legume-based fermented foods remains poorly understood, particularly under reduced-salt conditions. This study evaluated the effects of substrate, salt concentration and fermentation time on the colour, textural properties and rheological behaviour of six alternative legume-based misos over 18 months of fermentation and compared their final properties with soybean reference misos. Misos were produced from chickpea, lupin and cowpea using conventional- and reduced-salt formulations containing 120 and 30 g salt/kg final product, respectively. Colour, textural and rheological properties were affected by substrate, salt concentration and fermentation time. Chickpea-based misos showed the most pronounced darkening, whereas lupin-based misos remained lighter and more yellow. Firmness and adhesiveness decreased mainly during the first 3 months, and reduced-salt misos were generally firmer and more adhesive than conventional-salt misos. Despite changes in viscoelastic moduli, all misos retained predominantly solid-like weak-gel behaviour throughout fermentation. At 18 months, the alternative legume-based misos differed from soybean reference misos but remained broadly comparable, although soybean misos were firmer. These findings further support the technological potential of chickpea, lupin and cowpea as alternative substrates for miso production using both conventional- and reduced-salt formulations, thereby contributing to the diversification of sustainable plant-based fermented foods.

works.title: Biogenic amines in meat products: formation, control, detection, and AI-assisted management—a narrative review
works.abstract: Biogenic amines (BAs) are low-molecular-weight nitrogenous compounds commonly found in meat products, and their excessive accumulation is associated with spoilage, quality deterioration, and potential health risks. This review summarizes the formation mechanisms, control strategies, detection approaches, and emerging artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted applications related to BAs in meat products. BAs formation mainly results from microbial decarboxylation of free amino acids and is affected by precursor availability, microbial activity and decarboxylases, as well as processing and storage conditions. Current control strategies, including starter cultures, natural bioactive compounds, and non-thermal technologies (e.g., high hydrostatic pressure (HHP), pulsed electric field (PEF), and cold plasma), are discussed for their effectiveness in reducing BAs accumulation. Conventional analytical techniques, such as high-performance liquid chromatography and liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, together with emerging rapid detection tools like fluorescent probes, biosensors, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), and surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS), are critically reviewed. Particular attention is given to AI-assisted applications in BAs detection, prediction and control. Key challenges, incomplete validation of simultaneous multi-amine methods, limited comparability among intervention studies, and the lack of sufficiently large datasets linking processing conditions to BAs changes. This review provides an updated reference for BAs management and meat quality and safety evaluation.

works.title: Regulatory mechanism of LuxS/AI-2 quorum sensing system on biofilm formation of Listeria monocytogenes on the surface of fresh-cut iceberg lettuce
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Listeria monocytogenes ( L. monocytogenes ) readily forms biofilms on the surfaces of leafy vegetables, but the regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the role and mechanism of the LuxS/AI-2-mediated quorum sensing (QS) system in biofilm formation by L . monocytogenes during its colonization of fresh-cut iceberg lettuce (FCIL). The study found that inoculation of L . monocytogenes on FCIL increased the production and accumulation of autoinducer-2 (AI-2), which was closely associated with the acceleration of the activated methyl cycle (AMC). Specifically, this acceleration was driven by enhanced activities of key enzymes and elevated metabolites content within the AMC, especially S-adenosyl-methionine (SAM), with its content reaching 2036.29 ng/g in the later stage of storage, thereby providing sufficient precursors for AI-2 synthesis. In addition, the addition of exogenous AI-2 (70 μmol/L) significantly promoted biofilm formation and development (the viable counts in the biofilm increased by 43.62%), enhanced bacterial autoaggregation, and upregulated the expression of biofilm-related genes. In summary, the LuxS/AI-2 QS system played a central role in regulating biofilm formation.

works.title: Effect of pectin/alginate shell composition on chitosan-core hydrogel beads for pH-responsive encapsulation
works.abstract: Core–shell hydrogel beads were fabricated from naturally derived polysaccharides to encapsulate red cabbage extract (RCE), which served both as a model bioactive extract and as an intrinsic pH-responsive visual probe for monitoring acid-induced color changes and compound redistribution within the beads. The beads consisted of a chitosan core and either pectin or pectin/alginate shells formed by alkaline-induced solidification of chitosan and Ca 2+ -mediated crosslinking of pectin or alginate. Increasing CaCl 2 concentration and bead-forming time increased the diameter and shell thickness, whereas alginate incorporation decreased these parameters but markedly increased hardness. Shell composition influenced structural integrity and acid-response behavior. The selected 90Pec10Alg formulation (pectin/alginate, 90:10) retained its bead-like structure across pH 1.0-12.0 while maintaining a blue core between pH 3.0 and 11.0. Incubation in DI water or HCl solution at pH 2.0 for 2 h generally reduced DPPH radical-scavenging activity, FRAP, and total phenolic content recovered from the bead cores. Comparison with free RCE indicated assay-dependent effects of encapsulation, with greater relative retention of DPPH radical-scavenging activity in the bead cores but no consistent improvement in FRAP or TPC. These findings demonstrate relationships among pectin/alginate shell composition, bead mechanical properties, acid-response behavior, and retention of encapsulated bioactives, supporting the potential of composite shells as adaptable platforms for pH-responsive encapsulation.

works.title: Optimization of vacuum impregnation of purple corn cob extract into Andean potato slices for the development of functional air-fried snacks
works.abstract: Purple corn cob is an anthocyanin-rich agro-industrial by-product with potential as a natural source of bioactive compounds for snack enrichment. This study optimized the vacuum impregnation (VI) of Andean potato slices with purple corn cob extract and evaluated the quality of the resulting air-fried snack. A three-factor, three-level Box–Behnken design was applied using vacuum pressure (40–80 kPa), treatment time (5–15 min), and anthocyanin concentration in the impregnation solution (500–1500 mg C3G/L) as independent variables. Total monomeric anthocyanins (TMA), total phenolic content (TPC), and antioxidant capacity (DPPH, ABTS, and ORAC) were used as response variables. Multi-response optimization identified 72 kPa, 15 min, and 1270 mg C3G/L as the optimal VI condition within the evaluated Box–Behnken experimental domain, with an overall desirability of 0.612. Experimental validation showed relative errors ranging from 1.82% to 15.97%. Compared with the non-impregnated air-fried control, the optimized snack showed higher TMA, TPC, DPPH, ABTS, and ORAC values, with increases of 83.5%, 106.7%, 356.3%, 119.2%, and 253.7%, respectively. These percentages represent relative increases in the final snack compared with the non-impregnated control, rather than anthocyanin retention during air-frying. VI also promoted solution uptake and color changes, resulting in a marked color difference between the optimized and control snacks (ΔE* = 39.1). Optimized VI combined with air-frying represents an effective strategy for producing bioactive-enriched potato snacks without added oil, while valorizing purple corn cob as a source of bioactive compounds.

works.title: Recombinant Production and Characterization of Novel Clostridium Autolysins for Inhibiting Clostridium tyrobutyricum
works.abstract: Clostridium tyrobutyricum is a major anaerobic spoilage bacterium responsible for late blowing defects in dairy products due to gas production during fermentation. This study aimed to clone, express, and evaluate two putative autolysin genes encoding a cell wall hydrolase ( ct-cwh ) and a peptidoglycan peptidase ( ct-cp ) from C. tyrobutyricum as targeted biocontrol agents. Both genes were cloned into the pQE-30 vector and transformed into various Escherichia coli hosts. By implementing an optimized heat shock-assisted induction strategy overnight at 25 °C in Luria–Bertani medium supplemented with 0.5 mol/L NaCl and 1 mmol/L betaine (LBNB) using E. coli SHuffle T7, both enzymes were effectively produced in soluble and functionally active form. Following nickel-nitrilotriacetic acid (Ni-NTA) affinity chromatography, production yields reached 10.75 mg/L for ct-cwh and 20 mg/L for ct-cp. Lysis assays revealed concentration-dependent lytic activity, with rapid cell wall degradation under physiological conditions (pH 7.0, 37 °C). Combining the enzymes produced greater lytic activity than either enzyme alone and almost completely suppressed C. tyrobutyricum -induced gas formation in an anaerobic milk-based model system. No lytic activity was detected against the non-target organism Lactococcus lactis. In conclusion, obtaining peptidoglycan hydrolases in soluble and active form remains a major challenge, and overcoming it for ct-cwh and ct-cp was a key achievement of this work. The purified enzymes specificallylysed C. tyrobutyricum and suppressed gas formation in a milk-based model; particularly in combination, they are highly promising candidates for the biocontrol of clostridial spoilage in the dairy industry.

works.title: Microbial community succession and metabolic remodeling during the solidification process of HuangShui
works.abstract: HuangShui (HS), a high-strength organic byproduct of sauce-flavor Baijiu fermentation, poses environmental risks if discharged untreated, yet its spontaneous liquid-to-solid transition offers reduction/reuse potential. Integrating 16S rRNA sequencing and untargeted metabolomics across four stages (HS0–HS3), we decoded microbial succession and metabolic remodeling. Achromobacter rose from 3.21% to 88.52% as dominant genus, while Virgibacillus , Oceanobacillus and Kroppenstedtia declined; evenness/richness peaked in HS1–2, fell at HS3, indicating two-phase succession (salt-tolerant → oligotrophic). Free amino acids peaked at 65.41 mg/g (HS2), organic acids at HS3, phenols/benzene derivatives at HS2, while alkaloids and lipids decreased. Crude fiber and protein strongly correlated with dominant genera, implicating them as succession drivers. KEGG revealed branched-chain amino-acid synthesis (HS1–2) and enhanced carbohydrate/amino-acid/nucleotide metabolism (HS2–3). Logistic Regression classified bacteria (accuracy 0.986) far better than metabolites (0.667), with reprogramming intensifying during solidification. This clarifies HS solidification ecology, supporting harmless, resource-efficient reuse.

works.title: Corrigendum to “Influence of different frozen temperatures and time on the oxidation reaction and mitochondrial integrity of pork” [LWT 231, (2025), 118249]
A Study on the Effects of Drying Methods on the Physical Properties, Flavor, and Other Quality Characteristics of Cooked Chickpeas
works.abstract: The development of plant-based snack foods places multidimensional demands on processing technologies, necessitating a balance of efficiency, texture, and flavor. To address this challenge, this study systematically evaluated the comprehensive effects of hot-air drying (HAD), vacuum microwave drying (VMD), and vacuum freeze-drying (VFD) on ready-to-eat chickpeas assessing their performance across three dimensions: drying efficiency, physical properties, and flavor. The findings revealed differential regulation patterns of product quality by different drying methods. The results showed that in drying chickpeas to essentially the same moisture content, VMD required the shortest processing time, representing a 97.6% reduction compared with HAD. In terms of physical quality, the VMD group exhibited plump seeds with a natural color, and a dense, uniform internal microstructure. It also showed the highest hardness and chewiness, imparting a firm and chewy texture to the product. GC-IMS identified a total of 53 VOCs. In the VMD group, the contents of characteristic esters, including n-butyl acetate and (-)-ethyl lactate, were significantly higher than those in the other treatment groups. This enrichment imparted a rich fruity aroma to the product. Moreover, the overall flavor profile of the VMD group was the closest to that of the control group. The PLS-DA model further corroborated that esters are the key biomarkers distinguishing flavor differences among the various drying methods. In summary, VMD can significantly enhance drying efficiency while maintaining excellent textural characteristics and flavor quality, providing a technically feasible and superior solution for the industrial production of ready-to-eat chickpeas and similar legume-based snack foods.

works.title: Effects of hot-air drying temperature and freeze-drying pre-treatment on the colour, texture, nutritional components and flavour metabolism of dried papaya slices
works.abstract: The different effects of hot-air and freeze drying on the overall quality of papaya remain unclear. This study compared the colour, texture, nutrient retention, and volatile organic compound (VOC) profiles of papaya slices subjected to hot-air drying (HAD) at 50, 60, and 70 °C and freeze drying (FD) with pre-freezing at −20 °C, −80 °C, and liquid nitrogen. Colorimetric and scanning electron microscopy results revealed that HAD caused severe browning ( Δ E up to 34.27) and > 90% hardness loss, whereas FD with liquid nitrogen pre-freezing (FD-LN) yielded the lowest Δ E (8.85) and best preserved the porous microstructure. FD-LN also achieved the highest carotenoid (55.34 μg/g DW) and ascorbic acid (2.65 mg/g DW) contents among all treatments. With respect to flavour attributes, a total of 692 VOCs were identified by HS-SPME-GC-MS and analysed by OPLS-DA (Q 2 > 0.93). HAD generated new volatile compounds (e.g., 2,3,5-trithiahexane) via Maillard reactions and lipid oxidation, while FD better retained native terpenoids (e.g., β-caryophyllene). These findings demonstrate that the pre-freezing protocol is a critical variable governing FD product quality and provide practical guidance for selecting drying conditions for high-quality dried papaya.

works.title: Cultivation-Dependent Modulation of Bioactive Metabolites and Antioxidant Activity in Indigenous Bangladeshi Ganoderma Mycelia
works.abstract: Submerged liquid fermentation provides a controllable, year-round alternative to fruiting-body cultivation of the medicinal mushroom Ganoderma , yet cultivation conditions and strains may markedly influence metabolite production and bioactivity. This study compared two previously unexplored indigenous Bangladeshi Ganoderma isolates, GS-3 (within the G. lucidum species complex) and GS-5 (within the G. carnosum lineage), cultivated in potato dextrose broth under shake-flask and static conditions that differed in agitation as well as medium volume, inoculum density, and duration to produce mycelial pellets (MP) and mycelial mats (MM), respectively. Methanolic extracts (MEs) of dried MP and MM were characterised by ATR-FTIR and GC–MS and evaluated for DPPH radical-scavenging activity with four-parameter logistic modelling. GC–MS profiling revealed cultivation-dependent metabolite variation, with 2,4-di- tert -butylphenol and methyl palmitate forming a conserved chemical core of GC-MS-detectable (volatile/semi-volatile) constituents shared by all four extracts, and methyl stearate present in three of the four. Static cultivation enriched the unsaturated lipid fraction in both strains and induced a distinctive methylated naphthalene cluster in GS-5, representing 43.6% of the curated chromatographic profile. Mean IC 50 values in the DPPH assay were lower for static-culture extracts (297–331 μg/mL) than shake-culture extracts (371–468 μg/mL). These findings demonstrate that strain identity and contrasting cultivation mode were associated with differences in methanolic chemotype and provide a basis for further investigation of indigenous Ganoderma biomass as a source of bioactive food ingredients.

works.title: Effects of chickpea flour incorporation and partial baking on nutritional, volatile, and sensory profiles of flatbreads
works.abstract: This study evaluated the effects of chickpea flour incorporation and baking conditions on the nutritional quality, volatile composition, and sensory acceptance of flatbreads. Wheat-based and wheat/chickpea (60:40) flatbreads were produced conventionally (REF), part-baked (PAR), or rebaked (REB). Chickpea incorporation improved nutritional value by increasing protein, dietary fibre, mineral content, and resistant starch, while reducing dough water absorption. Processing had limited impact on overall composition, although rebaking slightly increased resistant starch. Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) analysis showed that formulation was the main driver of volatile differences, with chickpea flatbreads exhibiting higher levels of aldehydes associated with green and grassy notes; rebaking further modified the volatile profile of both formulations, although this change was perceptible in odour discrimination tests only for the chickpea flatbreads. Consumer liking was driven by soft, smooth, elastic, and bread-like textures, whereas dryness, aftertaste, and difficult chewing reduced acceptance. Chickpea flatbreads received significantly lower liking scores than wheat controls, although liking did not differ significantly among the chickpea samples despite the aroma changes induced by rebaking. These findings highlight chickpea flour as a promising ingredient for nutritionally enhanced flatbreads, while partial baking may support quality and reduced retail food waste through on-demand finishing.

works.title: Open-bucket hand-milking of yaks on the Tibetan Plateau: An unaddressed food-safety risk in the raw-milk supply chain
Genome sequencing and comparative transcriptomics reveal the response of CAZymes in Coprinus comatus fruiting bodies to postharvest storage
works.abstract: Carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes) play a crucial role in the quality deterioration of Coprinus comatus fruiting bodies. However, a systematic investigation into the response of CAZymes to postharvest storage remains lacking. In this study, the genome of C. comatus strain Tebai39 (TB39) was de novo sequenced and assembled, resulting in a 35.69 Mb genome sequence. Following functional annotation of the genes, a CAZyme repertoire comprising 491 candidate genes was constructed for the first time. Subsequently, comparative transcriptomic analysis was performed to evaluate the differential expression of CAZymes in C. comatus TB39 fruiting bodies stored for varying durations. A total of 251 CAZyme genes were differentially expressed, including 107 glycoside hydrolases (GHs), 61 auxiliary activities (AAs), 27 carbohydrate-binding modules (CBMs), 26 carbohydrate esterases (CEs), 21 glycosyltransferases (GTs), and 9 polysaccharide lyases (PLs). CAZymes primarily regulate polysaccharide degradation by mediating the GH18, GH3, AA3_2, AA1_1, CE16, CE4, PL14_4, and CBM1 families, as well as polysaccharide biosynthesis by mediating the GH16, GT20, and CBM13 families. Collectively, these CAZymes contribute to nutrient loss, cell wall degradation, and mushroom browning, thereby driving the quality deterioration of postharvest C. comatus TB39.

works.title: Freezing-Induced Structural Changes in Egg White Proteins and Their Impact on Foaming Properties
works.abstract: This study investigated the effects of frozen storage on the foaming characteristics of egg white (EW) by characterizing the foaming performance of EW as well as the physicochemical properties and structure of EW proteins (EWPs). Freezing initially decreased the foaming capacity of EW by approximately 50%, followed by partial recovery, whereas foam stability increased by 82% during frozen storage. These changes were accompanied by increases in turbidity, average particle size, surface hydrophobicity, and apparent viscosity, together with a decrease in free sulfhydryl content. The protein secondary structure revealed decreases in β-sheet and α-helix contents, along with increases in random coil and β-turn content. Scanning electron microscopy revealed the formation of larger and more irregular protein aggregates after freezing. Correlation analyses suggest that freezing-induced conformational rearrangement and intermolecular association may contribute to the observed changes in foaming behaviour. These results indicate that freezing-triggered changes in protein conformation and intermolecular interactions are correlated with EWP aggregation, which may account for the observed shifts in EW foaming properties.

works.title: Monitoring, transfer dynamics and risk assessment of perchlorate and chlorate in Chrysanthemum morifolium Ramat
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Perchlorate and chlorate are inorganic oxyanion contaminants, and their processing fate in Chrysanthemum morifolium Ramat ( C. morifolium ) products remains uncharacterized, unlike that of the synthetic pesticides previously quantified in this commodity. In a market survey of 107 C. morifolium samples by UPLC-MS/MS, perchlorate was detected in 96.3% of samples (median 289.7 μg/kg), whereas chlorate was detected in 51.4%. Controlled kill-green processing reduced both contaminants by 10.0-16.4%, bud-type flowers retaining marginally higher residues than petal-type flowers, a morphological disparity smaller than that previously reported for pesticides. Subsequent drying and accelerated storage caused negligible changes, with processing factors of 0.943-1.087. Because of their high water solubility, brewing across three successive infusions mobilized nearly all residues into the infusion, with cumulative transfer efficiencies approaching 100%. Within the scenarios examined, dietary exposure modeling for multiple consumer populations, incorporating the measured transfer rate and an upper-percentile residue scenario, yielded hazard indices far below unity (0.120 for children); this held across a two-way sensitivity grid (0.028-0.545), a probabilistic simulation (95th-percentile HI 0.074-0.232) and a nine-source uncertainty analysis. These results demonstrate that post-harvest processing alone cannot mitigate exposure and that source-oriented control is essential. This work extends our previous pesticide dissipation dataset and supports differentiated safety criteria for inorganic and organic residues in herbal teas.

works.title: One-hour hydration improves interfacial stability and mitigates protein-lipid oxidation in liquid infant formula emulsions under accelerated oxidative stress
works.abstract: This study investigated the effects of protein hydration time during pretreatment on the physicochemical stability and protein–lipid co-oxidation of liquid infant formula (LIF) emulsions under a Fenton-type accelerated oxidative stress model. Emulsions prepared with different hydration times ranging from 5 min to 12 h were evaluated in terms of droplet characteristics, protein structure, emulsifying properties, interfacial behavior. Oxidative susceptibility was further evaluated using a Fenton-type accelerated oxidative stress model. The results showed that 1 h hydration provided the most favorable overall performance. Droplet size decreased from 509 nm to 283 nm, accompanied by improved dispersion and physical stability. The α-helix and random coil contents reached 15.6% and 33.90%, respectively, while the β-sheet and β-turn contents decreased to 31.1% and 19.4%. The O-H/N-H stretching band shifted from 3442.59 cm −1 to 3421.50 cm −1 , indicating strengthened hydrogen-bond interactions. Correspondingly, EAI and ESI reached 82.35 m 2 /g and 99.66%, respectively. Under accelerated oxidative stress, the 1 h hydrated emulsions exhibited the lowest levels of protein and lipid oxidation markers, including carbonyls, N-formylkynurenine, peroxide value, and malondialdehyde. Correlation analysis further indicated coordinated changes between protein and lipid oxidation. Overall, one-hour hydration provided the most favorable balance between interfacial stability and lower relative oxidative susceptibility of LIF emulsions under the Fenton-type accelerated oxidation model, highlighting hydration control as a practical pretreatment strategy for improving LIF emulsion stability.

works.title: Potential of Zymomonas mobilis as Non-Yeast for Blueberry Wine: A Comparative Case Study
works.abstract: Microbial strains play an important role in blueberry wine fermentation. The widespread use of Saccharomyces cerevisiae in blueberry wine fermentation leads to homogenized flavors. In this study, Zymomonas mobilis , an excellent non-yeast ethanologen, was compared with S. cerevisiae to evaluate its potential for blueberry wine fermentation. The metabolite contents in blueberry wines fermented with Z. mobilis differed from those inoculated with yeasts: Most remarkably, methanol content was significantly lower, and total phenolic content was significantly increased. Among volatile compounds, the concentrations of esters, alcohols, phenols, acids and terpenes decreased, while aldehydes and ketones increased significantly. Additionally, the wine fermented with Z. mobilis was rich in sorbitol. Metabolic pathway analyses further revealed that such significant differences were mainly involved in the metabolisms of amino acids, citrate cycle, and lipid. These findings suggest Z. mobilis as a potential alternative to traditional brewing yeast in blueberry and other fruit wine production.

works.title: Corrigendum to “The role of pigs and slaughterhouses in the transmission of Listeria monocytogenes into the meat processing chain” [Food Microbiol. 142 (2027) 105273]
Matrix-Dependent Growth and Community Dynamics of Spoilage-Associated Lactic Acid Bacteria in Weak Organic Acid Salt-Treated Conventional and Hybrid Ready-to-Eat Chicken Breast
works.abstract: Hybrid meat products are an emerging food category, but their microbial ecology during refrigerated storage remains poorly characterized. This study investigated the effects of commonly used weak organic acid salts on microbial community dynamics in conventional and hybrid uncured deli-style chicken breast products during refrigerated storage. Both product types were processed, packaged, inoculated with the same five-strain lactic acid bacteria (LAB) cocktail, and stored under identical conditions. LAB populations and pH were monitored, while bacterial community dynamics were characterized using Oxford Nanopore full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing, enabling high-resolution tracking of spoilage-associated taxa within the inoculated consortium over time and across treatments within matrix. Conventional and hybrid chicken breast exhibited distinct early taxonomic profiles and temporal shifts in microbial community composition within each matrix. LAB population responses to weak organic acid salt treatments differed between matrices over storage. At day 14, NaLD reduced LAB populations relative to the corresponding Control by approximately 1.59 and 1.27 log CFU/mL rinse in conventional and hybrid chicken breast, respectively, with a significant 0.32-log-CFU/mL-rinse difference between treatment effects ( P = 0.033). Sequencing further characterized treatment-associated microbial community dynamics within each matrix, with LAB predominating during later storage. Overall, these findings show that hybrid formulations can alter spoilage-associated taxonomic dynamics, including responses of the inoculated LAB consortium, even under the same processing and storage conditions, and underscore the need for matrix-specific validation of preservation strategies in hybrid meat products.

A UV mutant library reveals a link between mitochondrial genome loss and succinate production during wine yeast fermentation
works.abstract: The wine industry must adapt to new climatic and societal challenges. For this, selected yeast strains, mainly Saccharomyces cerevisiae , is a powerful lever, with ultra-violet (UV) mutagenesis used successfully to generate genetic diversity for strain improvement. From a library of 502 mutants, phenotyped in wine conditions, we identified a bimodal distribution of certain primary metabolites production. Using a multi-scale fermentation approach (15 mL screening, 250 mL validation and 1 L characterization), we compare 10 low and 10 high succinate producers, under wine-like conditions. Primary metabolite profiles differed markedly, particularly in the production patterns of tricarboxylic acid cycle intermediates, with a twofold and threefold differences in succinate and α-ketoglutarate production respectively. Pyruvate and α-ketoglutarate accumulated earlier in low-succinate-producing strains, whereas succinate production was delayed, occurring mainly after the stationary phase. These patterns suggest altered TCA activity and are consistent with a model in which early pyruvate and α-ketoglutarate accumulation precedes later succinate production, although this proposed pathway sequence was not directly measured. Genomic analysis of 5 high and 5 low succinate producers revealed complete absence of the mitochondrial genome, potentially resulting in the absence of the respiratory chain. However, mitochondrial genome loss cannot alone explain the phenotype, as UV mutagenesis may also have generated other genomic and genetic changes. Our results suggest an association between mitochondrial genome status and organic acid production. We hypothesize that changes in redox balance, potentially involving fumarase activity and cofactor reoxidation, could contribute to the observed profiles; these mechanisms were not directly measured.

Antifungal effect of Bacillus velezensis BLS-7 on postharvest internal decay of chestnut and its potential antifungal mechanisms
works.abstract: Chestnut Inner Rot Disease (CIRD), a serious postharvest disease caused by multiple fungal pathogens, leads to substantial economic losses in the chestnut industry. Microbial biocontrol offers a safe and effective strategy. In this study, targeting four dominant CIRD pathogenic strains previously isolated, a bacterial strain identified as Bacillus velezensis BLS-7 was isolated from chestnut-cultivated soil. BLS-7 exhibited strong antifungal activity against Diaporthe phaseolorum , Colletotrichum siamense , Fusarium culmorum , and Lasiodiplodia theobromae , with inhibition rates of 84.51% to 96.89%. Moreover, it demonstrated broad-spectrum antagonism against 14 tested pathogenic fungi, all with inhibition rates exceeding 64%. In vivo assays further verified the significant biocontrol efficacy of BLS-7 across different chestnut varieties. Whole-genome sequencing analysis revealed that the BLS-7 genome harbors 13 gene clusters associated with secondary metabolite synthesis. Through headspace solid-phase microextraction combined with Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (HS-SPME-GC–MS), the volatile organic compounds (VOCs) of BLS-7 were analyzed, identifying hexyl butyrate as a candidate key inhibitory monomer. This compound inhibited three of the four CIRD pathogens by over 80% in vitro and all four in chestnut assays, with maximum inhibition rates of 82.95% and 75.3%, respectively. Both the VOCs and hexyl butyrate produced by BLS-7 suppressed mycelial growth and sporulation by disrupting hyphal morphology. VOCs and hexyl butyrate also restricted fungal spread on chestnuts and delayed fruit quality deterioration. This work proposes a fumigation-mediated VOC strategy using hexyl butyrate as a candidate key effector against multi-pathogen chestnut rot, offering a promising approach for nut crop postharvest biocontrol.

Comparative evaluation of turbidity and impedance microbiology for rapid quantification of Bacillus cereus in skim milk under different temperatures, salt levels, and incubation times
Development of Meyerozyma caribbica Based Biocapsules as Encapsulating Matrices for Hydrophobic Compounds
works.abstract: Abstract The development of sustainable biocapsules using non-conventional yeasts (NCYs) within a circular bioeconomy represents a promising strategy for protecting volatile bioactive compounds. This study aimed to isolate a novel NCY strain from fruit and vegetable residues (FVR), optimize its biomass production, and develop biocapsules as encapsulating matrices for oregano essential oil (OEO) and carvacrol (CA). Meyerozyma caribbica RFH001 was isolated from domestic FVR and molecularly identified by sequencing of the internal transcribed spacer (ITS) region. Biomass production in Yeast Peptone Dextrose broth yielded 4.30 g/L with a productivity of 0.179 g/L.h. Biocapsules were obtained through NaCl-induced hyperosmotic plasmolysis, generating a hollow intracellular cavity while preserving cell integrity. Successful terpene encapsulation was confirmed by UV-Vis and FTIR-ATR spectroscopy, which revealed the characteristic fingerprint bands of CA (2988, 1501–1455, and 827 cm⁻¹) within the loaded matrices. Transmission electron microscopy revealed a pronounced expansion of the periplasmic space and a significant thickening of the cell wall fabric, which increased from 0.073 µm in empty biocapsules to 0.121 µm and 0.126 µm for OEO and CA microformulations, respectively ( p < 0.0001). In vitro antimicrobial assays demonstrated robust controlled-release dynamics; encapsulated CA displayed minimum inhibitory concentrations ranging from 3 to 12.5 mg/mL, exerting bactericidal effects against Staphylococcus aureus , Bacillus cereus , and Micrococcus luteus . Conversely, a bacteriostatic response was observed against Escherichia coli . This study provides the first evidence that biocapsules derived from FVR-isolated M. caribbica RFH001 can be employed as efficient, low-cost, and bio-based carriers for the stabilization and targeted delivery of hydrophobic antimicrobial agents.

Supercritical CO2 Valorisation of Oat Okara: Sequential Extraction of Lipids and Bioactive Phenolics
works.abstract: This study demonstrates a food-safe (GRAS) supercritical carbon dioxide (SC-CO 2 ) valorisation strategy for oat okara through sequential defatting and recovery of avenanthramides and phenolic compounds in a one-pot system. SC-CO 2 processing successfully removed 72% of the native lipids, while improvements in protein content (15%), total phenolic content (24%), and antioxidant capacities (FRAP 16%, DPPH 19%). Water- and oil-holding capacities of defatted oat okara were also enhanced, while its emulsion properties were maintained. Subsequent pressurised fluid extraction evaluated solvent composition (100% ethanol, 70% ethanol (v/v), water) and pressure (100–400 bar). Extraction with 70% ethanol at 200 bar provided highest overall phenolic yield and antioxidant capacity. Phenolic extraction also demonstrated a pressure-dependent response, with avenanthramides showing the highest recovery at 100 bar, whereas p-coumaric acid and ferulic acid were highest at 200 bar. SC-CO 2 valorisation of oat okara with sequential extraction is a novel integrated process offering for converting oat processing side-streams into high-value functional food ingredients.

Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses reveal monoterpenoid biosynthesis in Aspergillus cristatus during tea infusion fermentation
works.abstract: Monoterpenoids are key contributors to the characteristic aromas of fermented tea, but their formation by Aspergillus cristatus remains unclear. In this study, liquid-state fermentation of a tea infusion was tracked through inoculation with A. cristatus , monoterpenoid profiles, sensory analysis, and transcriptomics were generated at three fermentation stages with or without glucose supplementation. A. cristatus promoted monoterpenoid accumulation as fermentation progressed, and glucose supplementation induced earlier and stronger accumulation of key odor-active compounds. Gas chromatography–olfactometry coupled with aroma extract dilution analysis and odor activity value analyses identified linalool, α -terpineol, geranial, neral, geraniol, citronellol, β -ocimene, nerol, and β -myrcene as major odor-active monoterpenoids in TG12. Transcriptomic analysis indicated activation of the MVA pathway, and AcGal4 was identified as a putative regulatory factor associated with Acerg20 and AcTPS . AcTPS was functionally validated in vitro as a nerol synthase. These findings could assist in the targeted regulation of sensory characteristics of fermented tea.

works.title: Machine learning reshapes the discovery-to-application pipeline of food-derived bioactive peptides: from sequence mining to functional foods
Emerging frontiers of photoacoustic imaging in food science: From spectroscopy to smart non-destructive quality assessment
works.abstract: Background Ensuring food quality and safety requires analytical methods capable of detecting adulterants, structural defects, and compositional variations without damaging the product. Techniques like chromatography, spectroscopy, hyperspectral imaging, X-ray, and MRI face trade-offs between chemical specificity, spatial resolution, penetration depth, and operational cost. Photoacoustic spectroscopy (PAS) and its extension into photoacoustic imaging (PAI) offer a unique hybrid solution by coupling optical absorption contrast with acoustic resolution, enabling deeper, label-free, non-destructive examination of heterogeneous and opaque food matrices. Scope and approach This review examines the transition from PAS to PAI, evaluating the principles, system components, imaging modalities, and computational enhancement strategies, including model-based reconstruction, machine learning, and deep learning frameworks that support high-resolution, quantitative imaging. It synthesizes advancements in excitation sources, ultrasound detection technologies, fluence correction, and signal-processing pipelines and contextualizes them within key food-quality applications. Comparative assessments highlight the strengths and limitations of PAI relative to conventional spectroscopic and imaging techniques. Key findings and conclusions PAI demonstrates considerable potential for food-quality and safety assessment by enabling real-time visualization of internal microstructures, moisture gradients, fat distribution, adulterants, and microbial or foreign-matter contamination with depth-resolved imaging capability that depends on the food matrix, excitation wavelength, and imaging modality. Emerging low-cost light sources and compact ultrasound transducers are positioned to support portable, standalone PAI systems, while AI-driven reconstruction and analysis significantly improve image reliability and feature extraction. By integrating photonics, acoustics, and computational intelligence, PAI represents a transformative, scalable approach for smart, non-destructive food monitoring, offering a pathway toward industrial deployment and enhanced supply-chain transparency.

works.title: From predictive models toward digital twins in food-grade valorization of agri-food side streams: A review and implementation roadmap
works.abstract: Background Agri-food side streams can supply dietary fibre, protein and bioactive compounds for food ingredients, but their variable composition complicates consistent recovery and formulation. Data-driven models could help manage this variability, yet their validation and readiness for real-time process control remain unclear. Scope and approach Two searches of English-language research published from 2018 to 2025 identified 35 studies on food-grade valorization of agri-food side streams and 63 on data-driven modelling in this field. Studies were first screened for eligibility and appraised for methodological reporting, and evidence was synthesized by recovery or product stage, model validation and measured food-relevant outcomes. Key findings and conclusions Fibre and polyphenol enrichment was the most common food-application pathway (18 of 35 studies). Reported outcomes included up to 64.53% protein recovery from brewers’ spent grain and a reduction in predicted glycaemic index from 70 to 60 Machine-learning models reported R 2 values of approximately 0.90–0.99. However, these results were obtained mainly from bench-scale, single-feedstock datasets evaluated offline, with limited validation across independent batches, sites, or operating conditions. The two evidence bases also remained largely disconnected: food-application studies documented food-relevant outcomes, whereas most modelling studies (56 of 63) addressed recovery rather than a food product. No included study combined continuous bidirectional coupling with a documented process intervention and subsequent verification of a food-relevant effect. Predictive modelling therefore did not equate to an operational digital twin. This review proposes a three-domain assessment framework encompassing sustainability, inclusivity and implementation access, and digital maturity. A complementary five-phase technology-readiness roadmap translates these domains into four measurable decision gates covering feedstock specification, independent-batch model validation, pilot-scale sensing within the intervention window, and verified control effects alongside cost and access metrics. The framework and roadmap remain untested. Future studies should therefore evaluate them in multi-batch pilot trials using calibrated sensors and predefined food-quality criteria.

Genomic epidemiology of azithromycin-resistant Salmonella London reveals plasmid-mediated multidrug resistance dissemination through pork production chains
works.abstract: Salmonella enterica serovar London (S. London) is an emerging foodborne pathogen associated with pork production systems. Azithromycin resistance in S. London threatens food safety and therapeutic options, yet its genomic epidemiology remains poorly characterized. We analyzed 945 global S. London isolates (1984-2024) using core-genome MLST, phylogenomic analysis, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Four major clades (C1-C4) and eight sub-clades were identified, with ST155 dominant (95.9%, 906/945). Sub-clade C1.1 represented an Asian-specific lineage enriched for mph(A)-mediated azithromycin resistance (62.1%), with all resistant isolates being multidrug-resistant. Resistance was driven by mph(A)-harboring MDR cassettes on IncFIB(K) plasmids flanked by mobile genetic elements. Phylogeographic analysis revealed a potential farm-to-fork transmission pattern, with pork production systems as the putative primary dissemination conduit. These findings highlight the role of food-animal production in selecting and spreading azithromycin-resistant S. London, underscoring the need for integrated food chain surveillance and antimicrobial stewardship in agriculture.

The cardiometabolic health effects of the hard cheese matrix
works.journal: Critical Reviews in Food Science and Nutrition
works.abstract: Total dairy intake is often associated with positive health outcomes, including reduced incidences of cardio metabolic disease. Dairy foods are diverse in their nutrient composition and structure, or "matrix", and less is known about the bioactive effects of individual dairy foods and their influences on human health. Cheese has a complex matrix that contains beneficial dairy proteins, bacteria, and micronutrients but also contains saturated fats and sodium, nutrients generally associated with unfavorable effects on cardiometabolic disease risk. The nutrient composition of cheese raises unique questions about the impact of cheese consumption on human health outcomes. The current literature suggests that cheese consumption as a whole food has positive or neutral effects on several cardiometabolic outcomes, likely driven by bioactive proteins, fats, micronutrients, and bacteria in the cheese matrix, and, interestingly, appears to be protective against the negative effects of sodium and saturated fats that are otherwise observed when consumed in nondairy products. However, further studies are needed to identify the specific components, structural characteristics, and molecular interactions in cheese that confer these health effects. This review discusses what is currently understood about the influence of the cheese matrix on human health, particularly cardiometabolic health, and the potential mechanisms mediating these effects.

Extreme weather enhances Arcobacter butzleri internalization in lettuce: implications for fresh produce safety
works.abstract: Although Arcobacter butzleri is increasingly detected in fresh produce, its internalization under climate-driven abiotic stress remains uncharacterized. We assessed A. butzleri internalization in iceberg and romaine lettuce under three irrigation regimes (optimal, drought, heavy rain) and three contamination levels (low, medium, high), quantified as log CFU/g of fresh produce. Leaf tissue consistently showed higher contamination than root across all conditions and cultivars. Heavy rain combined with high contamination produced the highest leaf levels recorded across all conditions: 43,350 ± 22,422 (iceberg) and 40,298 ± 28,283 (romaine) CFU/100 g of fresh produce. Drought significantly increased leaf internalization in both cultivars at medium and high contamination. Most strikingly, romaine root internalization under drought at the medium level reached 1768 ± 632 CFU/100 g, an ∼13-fold increase over optimal irrigation (133 ± 27 CFU/100 g). These findings indicate that extreme weather amplifies A. butzleri internalization in lettuce, posing an underappreciated food safety risk beyond the reach of current surface decontamination methods.

High-voltage cold plasma alleviates chilling injury in green pepper by synergistically regulating antioxidant and membrane lipid metabolism
works.abstract: Green pepper ( Capsicum annuum L.) is prone to chilling injury (CI) during cold storage at 4 °C, causing quality deterioration. This study investigated the alleviating effect and physiological basis of high-voltage cold plasma (HVCP) on postharvest CI in green pepper. Fruits were treated with HVCP at 50 kV for 30–150 s and stored at 4 °C for 12 days. The 50 kV/60 s condition was most favorable, reducing the CI index by 94.74% and weight loss by 73.54%, while delaying deterioration of texture, color, and chlorophyll content. HVCP induced an early, transient, and reversible moderate accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS); H₂O₂ and O₂⁻ contents increased by 15.59% and 89.82%, respectively, compared with the control on day 2. It also activated the antioxidant enzyme system and ascorbate-glutathione (AsA-GSH) cycle at the transcriptional level, inhibited key enzymes involved in membrane lipid degradation, reduced phospholipid degradation and polyunsaturated fatty acid oxidation, and increased fatty acid unsaturation (U/S ratio) by 22.17% at the end of storage. Correlation and principal component analyses confirmed that HVCP enhanced chilling tolerance by coordinately regulating antioxidant defense and membrane lipid homeostasis, supporting its potential as a green non-thermal preservation technology.

works.title: Profiling of pollen in honey using multispectral imaging flow cytometry
works.abstract: Pollen identification from honey (melissopalynology) is of great economic and consumer relevance. Traditional microscopy is time-consuming and dependent on expert knowledge, thus limiting high-throughput analyses. We tested whether pollen images generated with Multispectral Imaging Flow Cytometry (MIFC) classified by machine learning (ML) (convolution neural networks (CNNs) and random forest (RF)) can serve as a fast and reproducible method for identifying pollen in honey. We examined how the classification of honey pollen is affected by images from different matrices (anther and honey samples), how results compare with traditional microscopic analysis and used a set of human-interpretable image features to better explain ML results. The study focused on the six common target pollen in honey Brassica, Castanea, Centaurea, Helianthus, Phacelia and Tilia type. A classifier trained with a combination of anther and honey brightfield and fluorescence images provided the best predictions for 13 monofloral and 10 polyfloral honeys. Yielding pollen identification results comparable to microscopy, three times more pollen can be evaluated, and a measurement time of a maximum of 10 min, the method demonstrates its high potential as a powerful screening tool in melissopalynology.

works.title: Matrix-derived hypoallergenicity: potential roles of Beta vulgaris polyphenols and betalamic acid in PR-10 allergen modulation
works.abstract: Cold-pressed apple, carrot, and celery juices retain native PR-10 allergens associated with Pollen-Food Allergy Syndrome, whereas thermal processing can alter allergen recognition while compromising heat-sensitive nutrients and sensory quality. We propose matrix-derived hypoallergenicity, a framework in which food-matrix chemistry may regulate allergen accessibility. Using beetroot ( Beta vulgaris ) as a model matrix, we examine two chemically plausible pathways, polyphenol-derived quinone modification and betalamic-acid-mediated carbonyl chemistry. Neither pathway has been validated in authentic juice systems. This perspective, therefore, defines a testable framework for modulating allergen behavior while preserving nutritional and sensory quality.

works.title: Trifluoromethylpyrimidine‑thiosemicarbazide derivatives as novel multifunctional food preservatives for enhancing storage stability of roxburgh rose juice
works.abstract: In this work, two predominant gas-generating spoilage fungi (labeled as CQ2 and CQ5) were isolated from deteriorated roxburgh rose ( Rosa roxburghii Tratt) juice and identified as Pichia nanzhaoensis and Arxiozyma slooffiae , respectively. Meanwhile, a series of novel trifluoromethylpyrimidine derivatives bearing a thiosemicarbazide group were synthesized. Biological activity evaluation demonstrated that compound 5a showed stronger antimicrobial efficacy against the isolated strains, with the EC 50 values of 10.63 μg/mL (CQ2) and 8.24 μg/mL (CQ5), respectively, than potassium sorbate (both exceeded 100 μg/mL); compound 5a also exhibited superior antioxidant activity, with the IC 50 values of 4.14 μg/mL (DPPH assay) and 2.95 μg/mL (ABTS assay), respectively, surpassing vitamin C (6.38 μg/mL) and trolox (8.04 μg/mL). Molecular docking and 100 ns dynamics simulations validated its stable binding to NADPH oxidase with the ΔE MMPBSA value of −36.458 kJ/mol, and ADMET analysis confirmed its desirable biosafety. In addition, application experiments confirmed that compound 5a effectively suppressed browning, conserved nutrients, and optimized the juice flavor of roxburgh rose juice during storage. Thus, these results suggest that compound 5a is a promising multifunctional preservative with integrated antimicrobial, antioxidant, and antibrowning activities for roxburgh rose juice and other fruit beverages.

The role of plant sterols in modulating the gut microbiota: implications for health and disease
works.abstract: Background Growing evidence indicates that plant sterols (PS) can promote health, partly by modulating gut microbiota (GM). However, no study has thoroughly synthesized PS-induced GM modulation across different pathophysiological contexts. Scope and approach This systematic review analysed 28 preclinical and clinical studies (4 in vitro , 21 animal models, and 3 clinical trials) to evaluate PS effects on GM composition and function across healthy status, lipid metabolism dysfunction, inflammation-colitis, and cancer models. Key findings and conclusions In healthy models, PS exhibited prebiotic activity by increasing health-associated genera, promoting preferential microbial metabolism of PS over cholesterol, and enhancing short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) production. In lipid metabolism dysfunction, PS consistently restored microbial diversity and modulated bile salt hydrolase-producing bacteria with modifications of bile acid metabolism. GM-related mechanisms also included enhanced SCFA production, improved intestinal barrier integrity, reduced trimethylamine generation, and cholesterol sulfonation. In colitis models, PS restored GM diversity increasing SCFA-producing genera. Antibiotic depletion negated protective effects, while faecal microbiota transplantation reproduced therapeutic benefits, providing direct evidence that GM mediates PS anti-inflammatory effects. In cancer models, PS restored GM composition towards non-tumour-bearing control levels despite severe baseline dysbiosis, with pronounced Lactobacillus enrichment and SCFA-induced antiproliferative effects demonstrated in vitro . Notably, specific taxonomic shifts and their functional implications varied substantially according to baseline metabolic status and disease context, highlighting the context-dependent nature of PS–GM interactions. However, clinical evidence remains limited and future research should incorporate comprehensive multi-omics approaches to confirm preclinical findings and establish context-specific dietary recommendations.

works.title: The potential role of dietary polyphenols in the management of gastrointestinal issues in autism spectrum disorder
works.journal: Critical Reviews in Food Science and Nutrition
works.abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental condition, frequently comorbid with heterogeneous gastrointestinal (GI) pathologies, including Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS), Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD), and functional motility disorders. Emerging evidence implicates the microbiota-gut-brain axis in the pathogenesis of these GI anomalies. Dietary polyphenols, characterized by potent antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neuromodulatory properties, represent a promising candidate approach for exploring the management of these comorbid conditions. This review critically examines the proposed molecular mechanisms by which specific phenolic compounds (e.g., resveratrol, quercetin and curcumin) may mitigate GI symptoms in ASD. Mechanistically, preclinical evidence suggests that polyphenols may help restore intestinal barrier integrity by upregulating tight junction proteins, suppress mucosal inflammation via the downregulation of Nuclear Factor Kappa B (NF-κB)/NOD-like Receptor Family Pyrin Domain Containing 3(NLRP3) pathways, and regulate gut motility through enteric neurotransmitter modulation. However, direct clinical efficacy in individuals with ASD remains largely unproven. Future clinical directions are proposed, focusing on the incorporation of low-fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides, and polyols (FODMAPs) natural food matrices and the development of controlled food fortification strategies over isolated high-dose supplementation. This work provides a theoretical foundation and a concise roadmap for advancing polyphenol-based dietary interventions in the management of GI pathophysiology in ASD.

works.title: Pine needles as a sustainable bioresource for agro-food industry
works.journal: Critical Reviews in Food Science and Nutrition
works.abstract: Recently, the interest in renewable plant-derived resources for the agro-food sector has significantly increased as industries seek green and sustainable bioprocess substrates. Pine needles (PN) are produced in large quantities across temperate and subtropical regions yet remain comparatively underexplored despite their cultural and medicinal uses. This review examines PN as a bioresource, focusing on botanical diversity, physicochemical composition (including 15-30% hemicellulose, up to 43% lignin and up to 60% cellulose), and secondary metabolite profiles. Particular attention is given to bioactive constituents such as phenolics (ranging between 9.8-14.1 mg GAE/g dried needles), flavonoids (ranging between 3.3-7.2 mg RE/g dried needles), and essential oils (reaching up to 0.8%, with 71 compounds identified in some species), along with relevance to food preservation, human nutrition, and health. The review evaluates bioprocessing approaches for saccharification and fermentation of PN lignocellulose and their potential integration into circular agro-food systems. This review comprehensively evaluates pine needles across different species, valorization in the food industry, highlighting the foremost knowledge in this domain. Despite promising opportunities, challenges remain, including regulatory guidelines, limited exploration in food applications and the recalcitrance of lignocellulosic biomass. By consolidating diverse research fields, the work establishes PN within future sustainable valorization frameworks for food and agricultural applications.

works.title: Fructose as a systemic metabolic signal orchestrating metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease pathogenesis
works.journal: Critical Reviews in Food Science and Nutrition
works.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects approximately 30% of the global population, yet the specific role of dietary fructose in disease progression remains inadequately defined. This review delineates the “Fructose-ectopic lipid accumulation (ELA)-MASLD” axis, identifying refined fructose (e.g., from sugar-sweetened beverages) not merely as a substrate but as a systemic signal that coordinates a pathological metabolic network. Hepatic fructose metabolism via the ketohexokinase-C (KHK-C) pathway bypasses the rate-limiting phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK-1) checkpoint, promotes unregulated de novo lipogenesis (DNL), ATP depletion, and organellar stress. We identify the functional decline of subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT) plasticity as an important driver of this lipotoxic cascade. This tends to result in systemic lipid spillover, promoting an inflammatory cascade that impairs the intestinal barrier and induces insulin resistance (IR) in skeletal muscle and bystander organs. Furthermore, we discuss how genetic variants amplify this toxicity and critically evaluate emerging preclinical hypotheses regarding epigenetic remodeling and transgenerational inheritance. Finally, we propose stratified management strategies that integrate evidence-based nutritional modifications with targeted pharmacotherapy, distinguishing between hepatic-dominant and adipose-derived lipid excess to optimize clinical outcomes.

works.title: Plant-derived exosome-like nanoparticles as candidate nano-prebiotics: from structure-enabled delivery to host–microbiota interface remodeling
works.journal: Critical Reviews in Food Science and Nutrition
works.abstract: Gut ecosystem homeostasis depends on coordinated interactions among commensal microorganisms, the mucosal barrier, and the immune system. Conventional prebiotics rely on selective utilization by host microorganisms, but their efficacy is shaped by baseline microbiota and disease-associated ecological constraints. Plant-derived exosome-like nanoparticles (PELNs) are naturally occurring membrane-bound nanoparticles characterized by source-dependent lipid interfaces and associated molecular components, including small RNAs, proteins, polysaccharides, and plant-derived metabolites. We evaluate selected PELNs within a provisional “candidate nano-prebiotic” framework that allows particle- or component-mediated mechanisms to coexist with microbial utilization of fermentable components without implying equivalence to consensus-defined prebiotics. We critically assess evidence for microbe-directed and host-mediated effects on microbial functions, microbiota-derived metabolites, epithelial barrier integrity, and mucosal immunity, particularly in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Current evidence remains heterogeneous and predominantly preclinical, with major uncertainties regarding particle identity, component-specific causality, in vivo fate, microbiota dependence, dose plausibility, and mechanistic generalizability. We further define conceptual boundaries among PELNs, conventional prebiotics, and engineered nano-prebiotics and identify priorities for standardization, causal testing, food-relevant exposure assessment, safety evaluation, and mechanistically informed human studies.

High Hydrostatic Pressure: A Tool for Functional Modification of Lupin Protein Isolates
works.abstract: Abstract This study aimed to evaluate high hydrostatic pressure (HHP) processing as a modification method for protein functionalization. Lupin protein isolates (LPI), derived from the species Lupinus luteus , were subjected to pressures of 200, 350, and 500 MPa for 10 min at 20 °C, and the impact of HHP on protein structure and techno-functional properties was studied. HHP treatments induced changes in both secondary and tertiary structures, resulting in partial protein unfolding. A decrease in fluorescence intensity along with increased surface hydrophobicity indicated partial unfolding and exposure of hydrophobic groups to the aqueous environment. Conformational changes also promoted the exposure of sulfhydryl groups, suggesting that the formation and/or rearrangement of intermolecular disulfide bonds may have contributed to protein aggregation, as supported by gel electrophoresis and reduced free sulfhydryl content at 500 MPa. However, particle size distribution indicated coexistence of dissociated/smaller species and larger aggregates rather than a uniform increase in particle size. These structural alterations were associated with increase in solubility and reduction in emulsifying activity. Pressures of 200 and 350 MPa decreased the least gelation concentration of LPI from 13 to 11%, indicating improved gelling capacity, and the viscoelastic results evidenced the formation of stronger gel networks, particularly at 350 MPa. HHP treatment at 500 MPa caused a less favorable effect in the gelling capacity compared to 350 MPa, likely due to further protein aggregation. Overall, the results demonstrated that HHP can be applied to modify the lupin protein structure and tailor its techno-functionality, promoting the use of lupin protein as a gelling agent in food matrices.

Research Progress on the Effects of Magnetic Field‐Assisted Treatment on the Texture, Color, and Enzyme Activity of Fruits and Vegetables
works.journal: Comprehensive Reviews in Food Science and Food Safety
works.abstract: Softening texture and fading color are the main reasons for the reduced marketability of freshly harvested fruits and vegetables, and these adverse quality changes are caused by a series of enzymatic reactions. Magnetic field treatment, as a promising nonthermal physical preservation technology, has excellent biological safety, zero chemical residue, and superior penetration performance, and is an effective strategy to alleviate the postharvest quality deterioration of fruits and vegetables. This paper systematically reviews the relationship between parameters such as magnetic field intensity, frequency, and duration of action and their preservation effects, discusses the current research limitations, and looks forward to the future exploration directions of molecular mechanisms and potential technological applications. The optimized magnetic field intervention can effectively inhibit the senescence process of fruits and vegetables after harvest and significantly suppress the activities of key catabolic enzymes, including pectinase, cellulase (Cx), peroxidase (POD), polyphenol oxidase (PPO), and lipoxygenase (LOX), thereby reducing the degradation of chlorophyll and carotenoids and delaying the degradation of cell walls, thus jointly maintaining the structural integrity and sensory quality of postharvest fruits and vegetables. It is worth noting that the biological effects of magnetic fields are bidirectional and exhibit a distinct "window effect." The same magnetic field treatment may either inhibit or activate the same enzyme, depending on the magnetic field parameters, fruit variety, and storage conditions. Moreover, when the parameters exceed the effective window range, the effect may reverse. The mechanism of magnetic field-mediated preservation mainly involves the regulation of enzyme conformation, the maintenance of intracellular free radical homeostasis, and the guarantee of the stability of the structure and function of the cell membrane of horticultural products. However, several key bottleneck problems remain unsolved. For instance, the molecular mechanisms that lead to species-specific responses remain unclear, and the data supporting large-scale industrial applications are still insufficient. This review provides a reference basis for promoting and improving magnetic field preservation technology.

works.title: Balancing flavor and bioactivity: fermentation-driven glucosinolate hydrolysis and sulforaphane stability in cruciferous vegetables
works.journal: Critical Reviews in Food Science and Nutrition
works.abstract: Cruciferous vegetables are rich in glucosinolates (GSLs) with diverse R-group side chains. Hydrolysis of GSLs yields various isothiocyanates (ITCs), including sulforaphane (SFN), which possesses anti-cancer and antioxidant activities. However, the pungent odor of SFN limits consumer acceptance. Probiotic fermentation effectively improves flavor and nutritional value. Single-strain fermentation may result in relatively monotonous flavors, whereas co-fermentation enriches flavor but may impair SFN stability. Microbial metabolism in co-fermentation can disrupt SFN-stabilizing acidic conditions and accelerate its degradation. Nevertheless, major research gaps still exist, including unclear microbial interactions in co-fermentation systems and bottlenecks for industrial-scale application. Based on GSL hydrolysis mechanisms, this review systematically compares single-strain and co-fermentation in terms of flavor and SFN content, and analyzes the mechanisms by which these two approaches improve the flavor of SFN-rich cruciferous vegetable juices. Furthermore, to quantify functional and flavor attributes under different fermentation processes and optimize product quality, we systematically summarize conventional and advanced detection techniques for flavor compounds and SFN. Meanwhile, the association between probiotic biotransformation and sensory quality in SFN-rich systems is specifically discussed, aiming to offer theoretical reference and practical insights for the quality improvement and product development of fermented cruciferous vegetable beverages.

A portable assay for on-site assessment of the phytopathogens affecting the storability and safety of agrifoods
works.abstract: This study reports the development and validation of portable optical sensor platforms for the on-site detection of fungal contamination in agri-food products. The systems combine an autonomous handheld reader with disposable optical sensor coatings integrated into vials or sachets and are operated under semi-selective conditions targeting mycotoxin-producing phytopathogenic fungi. Performance was evaluated under laboratory conditions using representative species of Aspergillus ( A. ochraceus , A. flavus , A. carbonarius ) and Penicillium ( P. verrucosum, P. expansum ) grown on semi-selective media and applied to artificially and naturally infected fruits and vegetables. The platforms were further validated in a semi-industrial setting using the table grape supply chain as a model, analysing fresh, dried, and liquid samples. The proposed approach provides a rapid alternative to conventional culture-based methods for microbial quality assessment, enabling faster detection of fungal contamination. Overall, the sensor system offers a non-destructive, rapid, and portable tool for improved monitoring of fungal contamination in agri-food chains, with potential to enhance batch release efficiency, reduce product losses, and support more frequent safety and hygiene assessments. Under laboratory conditions, the estimated 24-h detection threshold concentration (LOD₅₀) was approximately 2 × 10 5 CFU/mL for the sachet format and 6 × 10 4 CFU/mL for the vial format.

Caco-2-derived spheroids and organ-on-a-chip for food safety risk assessment: mechanisms of intestinal inflammation induced by 20 nm polystyrene nanoplastics
works.abstract: Microplastics released from food packaging have become an emerging food safety concern and may contribute to intestinal inflammation. This study employed Caco-2-derived spheroids combined with self-developed microfluidic organ-on-a-chip technology to systematically investigate the effects of 20 nm polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs) on oxidative stress and functional homeostasis in the three-dimensional (3D) intestinal epithelial microenvironment. We detected oxidative stress markers, antioxidant capacity, inflammatory factors, and epithelial function indicators; evaluated Villin and ZO-1 expression by immunofluorescence staining; performed metabolomic analysis on chip effluents; conducted styrene-based computational target prediction and exploratory molecular docking, identifying ALOX5 as a computational candidate; and independently analyzed a public IBD single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset using in silico ALOX5 perturbation for exploratory analysis. The results demonstrated that 40 μg/mL and 400 μg/mL PS-NPs could induce oxidative, inflammatory, and epithelial-associated alterations. This study is the first to integrate Caco-2-derived spheroids and organ-on-a-chip for nanoplastic toxicity evaluation, which provides a novel experimental platform and theoretical basis for investigating potential mechanisms underlying nanoplastic toxicity and risk assessment of food-related nanoplastics.
